notes.title: Let's Play Together - Country Side
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/3036e6e36e63ce479ce2c6d5083a325d2726f297.png"][/img][/p][p]Hello friends! Every Friday 17:30 UTC/GMT - we hold a “Let’s play together” competition. During next 24 hours everyone is welcome to try and score the best time in a preselected level. Join our Discord server and keep Discord running while playing — your results will be automatically published in the #lets-play-together channel. [u]You need to get 5 stars to qualify.[/u][/p][p][/p][p]Glittering prizes include:[/p][p]1) Top 3 winners receive one random card each. Collect 18 locomotive cards and advance to next set of 8 all new cards! Complete that second set and enter a final tier of 12 rare cards! Assemble all cards from all tiers and receive a special prize. Easy![/p][p]2) Every player registered by our Discord bot has a chance to get a card. The number of cards depends on the number of participants: one additional card for every 10 train connoisseurs on the list. More players means more prizes![/p][p]2.5) One non-Champion from the top 10 gets a Challenger Card - introduced along with 12 new loco cards from Myths And Rails and Editor's Bulletin![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/da8f894851a5b1d8e435fac676c6a5309d381e2b.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Visit our [url="https://discord.gg/train-valley"]Discord server[/url] (#lets-play-together channel) to learn more.[/p][p][/p][p]A level we are playing this week is [/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3566637179"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][/p][p]Now open your game - the link is right there in the main menu.[/p][p][/p][p]Good luck everyone![/p]

notes.title: Train Valley 2 is on sale!
notes.notes:
[p]Train Valley 2 is on for daily deal - stock up on our trainful puzzles about train driving at a -80% discount, starting today!   [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/602320/Train_Valley_2/"][/dynamiclink]We're also adding a fix for a possible Steam cloud bug that prevented you from keeping your progress after playing on another PC.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Important - skip the following instructions if your cloud sync is working fine. [/b]If not:

1. Click your game in the Library list - Properties - General tab and add [b]-force-cloud[/b] in the Launch Options text field.
2. If you already have some launch options applied just add this new one with a space.
3. Close the window.[/p][p][/p][p]Tell your friends![/p][p]


[/p][h3][b][url="https://discord.com/invite/train-valley"]Discord[/url]🖥️[url="https://twitter.com/trainvalley"]Twitter / X[/url] 🖥️[url="https://www.facebook.com/trainvalley/"]Facebook[/url][/b][/h3]

notes.title: Locomotive 1-9 (The Ministry)
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/2a377a0d682c535197ea6f0dfcc169648c5689e8.jpg[/img]([b]C53 43 pulling the Tsubame train, photographed between Okubo and Akashi on December 9, 1934. Notice peculiarly similar approach to streamlining, even though the first A4, LNER 2509 "Silver Link" didn't enter service until 7th September 1935.[/b] [i]- Katsusaburo NISHIO / 西尾克三郎 - Scanned from p.34 of "Railway Pictorial" No.426, [url=https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9B%BD%E9%89%84C53%E5%BD%A2%E8%92%B8%E6%B0%97%E6%A9%9F%E9%96%A2%E8%BB%8A#/media/%E3%83%95%E3%82%A1%E3%82%A4%E3%83%AB:JGR_C5343_hauling_train.jpg]from Wikipedia[/url][/i])

They say the first step is always the hardest. Class C53 may be considered that first step on Japan's way to perfecting its passenger rail transportation. Disliked by the crews and flawed by design, expensive and short-lived, Japan's only non-experimental three-cylinder locomotive was Hideo Shima's debut project. It is believed that the streamlining treatment of one C53 unit provided crucial data that would later be collated into the creation of the Shinkansen in 1964.

[h2]Shigosan ("C53" in Japanese)[/h2]

In February 1926, amidst growing demand for faster passenger trains with more room and better safety standards it was concluded the C51 locomotive has come to its theoretical limits of performance and it was time to introduce a completely new technology, Ministry of Railways decided to import six ALCo (American Locomotive Company)-built locomotives - classified as C52 - to sample a three-cylinder Gresley conjugated valve gear that was under development in Europe and the United States at the time. The last Japanese steam locomotives to be imported, these were subjected to various test and after showing an increase in performance served as an example for the future C53 design. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/1fba8462aa2d105cc84fc442b26013182227ce3a.jpg[/img]([b]Builder's photo of Japanese Government Railways C52 three-cylinder Pacific locomotive[/b] - [i]American Locomotive Company ALCO Historic Photos - Steam Locomotive Development in Japan [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JNR_Class_C52#/media/File:C52_(8200).jpg]from Wikipedia.[/url][/i])

A total of 97 Class C53 locomotives were built by Kawasaki Heavy Industries Rolling Stock Company and Kisha Seizo between 1928 and 1929 to haul Tōkaidō Main Line express services, such as the Tsubame and the Fuji, which connected Tokyo and Osaka, the country’s two largest cities. 

There were a number of issues with the Gresley gear. Because of its complexity routine maintenance took a lot more time and effort, but the main difficulty was that sustained high speed running could sometimes cause parts wear rapid enough for the system to destroy itself. LNER Class A4 4468 Mallard suffered that same malfunction during its world speed record run and was forced to limp back to its depot for repairs afterwards. It should also be noted that Japanese engineers did not yet possess an intimate understanding of the technology and the excessive emphasis on C53's weight reduction caused problems of its own such as frequent cracks due to insufficient rigidity of components.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/bbd39e5cd8869a6f619385c0170ef05c8530be57.jpg[/img]([b]C53 10[/b] - [i]by user 鉄道情報社 - 機関車形式写真帖  [url=https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9B%BD%E9%89%84C53%E5%BD%A2%E8%92%B8%E6%B0%97%E6%A9%9F%E9%96%A2%E8%BB%8A#/media/%E3%83%95%E3%82%A1%E3%82%A4%E3%83%AB:JGR-C53SteamLocomotive.jpg]from Wikipedia.[/url][/i])

Although the issue could be contained in a peacetime environment - indeed, many crews noted that when properly maintained and tuned, driving a C53 was more comfortable than the subsequent C59 and C62 types because of its low vibration due to the three cylinders operating at equal intervals, a wide and comfortable cab, a boiler with good steam flow, and strong traction. Unfortunately, this class proved to be poorly suited to the rigors of heavy running and low maintenance levels of World War II.
Subsequently introduced precise alignment of the valve gear and new standards for manufacture and lubrication effectively solved the problems, but it was too late for C53s.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/e4e622915056e39b2453d01c6154993df3bb178f.jpg[/img]([b]C53 96 passing by Nagoya Station[/b] - you will visit the station during the events of Japanese Trails. - [i]Unknown author, duplicated by user kyu3 (124201) from Komaki, Aichi prefecture, Japan [url=http://photozou.jp/photo/show/124201/237844739]ゲートタワーの工事現場沿いの壁（？）に、昔の名古屋駅の写真 - 3：昭和12年の名古屋駅[/url][/i])

Although several locomotives were modified through the course of their service to address cinder accumulation and change exhaust pattern, all locomotives of the class were withdrawn by 1950 with the ongoing Tokaido line electrification and introduction of the C59 type.
Today, only one Class C53 locomotive has been preserved - C53 45 - and can be visited at the Kyoto Railway Museum.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/a350438924ddf31dd6dab1416bb2130a9ea80159.jpg[/img]
([b]C53 45 preserved at Umekoji Steam Locomotive Museum in December 2011[/b] - [i]by user LERK [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JNR_Class_C53#/media/File:Japanese-national-railways-C53-45-20111213.jpg]from Wikipedia.[/url][/i])

[h2]The Ministry[/h2]

Unfortunately C53 43 - the only streamlined locomotive of the class - could not be preserved, we only have pictures left. These pictures give us plenty reasons for its popularity with train modelists though.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/137ed607d631484e9607ebbf8d1f21f79e03138f.jpg[/img]
([b]Plarail JNR C5341 side by side with [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/602320/view/3199256688972572101]a rotary snowplow[/url][/b] [i]as seen in a  [url=https://paypayfleamarket.yahoo.co.jp/item/z406906890]Yahoo flea market listing[/url][/i])

In November 1934, C53 43 assigned to Umekoji was streamlined on a trial basis in a 20-day rush job at Takatori Works, following the worldwide streamlined locomotive boom. The front part of the smokehouse was cut at an angle, the driver's cab was replaced with an enclosed one, the entire car body and the upper part of the coal car were covered with streamlined steel plates, and the gap between the locomotive body and the coal car was covered with a hood. The exposed steam whistle was also fitted with a streamlined box. The paint color was prawn-brown.

Although the trend advocated a lot of drag reduction effects, at the operating speeds of less than 100 km/h (62 mph) the effect of drag on a running train was negligible. Rather, the goal was to improve the air flow around the train, prevent smoke from engulfing the passenger cars and reduce wind pressure on oncoming trains and passengers waiting on station platforms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/d0e4fca3971e3f75a427019f64d844861feabe0e.png[/img]
([b]C53 43 undergoing streamlining treatment[/b] [i] - added by user Leeferr	  [url=https://locomotive.fandom.com/wiki/JNR_Class_C53/Gallery]to the Locomotive Wiki[/url][/i])

After its completion, C53 43 made an official test run on November 24 at Takatori Works, and from December 1 of the same year until the timetable revision on July 1, 1937, when the C53s at Umekoji were withdrawn from express operation, it pulled the Tsubame train between Kobe and Nagoya (also pulling the outbound train between Akashi Yard and Kobe) and the Fuji train between Nagoya and Osaka. It also pulled express trains between Kyoto and Kobe.

In June 1935, performance tests were conducted between Hara and Suzukawa (present-day Yoshiwara) on the Tokaido Main Line using C53 43 and non-streamlined C53 55 at around 100 km/h (62 mph) with the performance test car connected. The results showed that drag coefficient for C53 43 was 87% of the conventional locomotive, so the company decided to streamline all C53s with 10 cars to be converted in 1935. The rear of the Tsubame coaches was also to be converted to a streamlined design to reduce aerodynamic drag further by 30%, These plans were never acted upon, with shortcomings like streamlined driver cabin that accumulated heat rather easily, increased maintenance and inspection times and a 3000 yen price of a single locomotive conversion cited.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/ea81514ad02ccd9b70d33bb322913b11a99cf7d9.jpg[/img]([b]Side view of the C53 43[/b] [i]- Katsusaburo NISHIO / 西尾克三郎 - Scanned from p.34 of "Railway Pictorial" No.426, [url=https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9B%BD%E9%89%84C53%E5%BD%A2%E8%92%B8%E6%B0%97%E6%A9%9F%E9%96%A2%E8%BB%8A#/media/%E3%83%95%E3%82%A1%E3%82%A4%E3%83%AB:JGR_C5343_sideview.jpg]from Wikipedia[/url][/i])

Hideo Shima will use knowledge he and his colleagues accumulated during the trials of C53 class and C53 43 while designing the C55 class locomotives, of which 20 were built streamlined.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/e01a04232700d192b3d0a2a71f59039b87dcd61d.png[/img]([b]JGR C5520 side view[/b] [i] - added by user Leeferr	  [url=https://locomotive.fandom.com/wiki/JNR_Class_C55]to the Locomotive Wiki[/url][/i])

Train Valley 2’s in-game counterpart is called The Ministry because Hideo Shima helped design Class C53 while employed by Ministry of Railways (Japanese Government Railways), and also to denote Japanese authorities' involvement and interest in the country's transportation system as well as the joint effort of many separate organizations they've arranged to produce C53s.

We have translated the wide streamline casing shape that covers every mechanism and leaves only boiler's reinforcement beams, a front hatch and a steam exhaust pipe to remind us this steamship looking vehicle is indeed a locomotive unto the in-game model and applied Train Valley 2's signature Tier 1 green livery. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/9daedecdf8e9d7c620701ebf44060cb644d073c1.png[/img]

We did our best preserving the wheel base configuration but we had to omit the tender. And before you ask - we made the front lights red because many train models tend to have these. We haven't found a single source that says C5343 did not have red lights :)

[h2]From steam engine to distributed-power multiple-unit control system[/h2]

Among the key people credited with the construction of the first Shinkansen are Hideo Shima, the Chief Engineer, and Shinji Sogō, the first President of Japanese National Railways (JNR) who managed to persuade politicians to back the plan. Other significant people responsible for its technical development were Tadanao Miki, Tadashi Matsudaira, and Hajime Kawanabe based at the Railway Technical Research Institute (RTRI), part of JNR. They were responsible for much of the technical development of the first line, the Tōkaidō Shinkansen. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/3a14ece4c1d30e459e9e909aaead0b7b221ffc78.jpg[/img]([b]JR East Shinkansen Lineup on a Public opening Event (the 30th Anniversary of the Jōetsu Shinkansen) at Niigata Shinkansen Rolling Stock Center. From the left - E5 Series, 200 Series, E4 Series, E2 Series, E3 Series, E926 Type (East i), and E1 Series[/b] [i] - added by user Rsa - Own work[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinkansen#/media/File:JR_East_Shinkansen_lineup_at_Niigata_Depot_201210.jpg] to Wikipedia[/url][/i])

As Hideo Shima said himself
[quote=] I started designing steam locomotives, but I always felt the limits of steam. On one hand, I wanted to build a steam locomotive with the greatest traction capacity to gain a reputation, but on the other hand, I repeatedly thought about what direction to take to pass the limits of steam, taking the features and condition of Japan into consideration.
...I was also thinking seriously how to meet JNR's transport needs. At that time, air and car traffic were showing remarkable growth. I thought that building a line that would soon fall behind the advancing transport world would be regrettable for the future of JNR and in meeting social expectations. I decided to build a railway that would be useful and rational for a long time into the future.[/quote]

Mr Shima organised the replacement of locomotive-hauled middle-distance trains on the Tokaido Line with electric railcar trains. This new EMU was nicknamed "Shonan Densha" and showed remarkable progress, with greatly improved running speed and excellent riding comfort surpassing the passenger cars hauled by locomotives. The speed increase made a day trip between Tokyo and Osaka possible. The super-express trains became able to make return trips and the economic advantages of the distributed-power system was clear. Soon, JNR had changed into one of the most prominent EMU-oriented railways in the world.

Mr Shima went on to overseeing the building of the first Shinkansen line in 1955. In addition to its innovative propulsion system, the Shinkansen also introduced features like air suspension and air-conditioning. Shima's team designed the sleek cone-shaped front from which the bullet train got its name. The cost of the first Shinkansen line also cost Shima his job. The building of the first line, which needed 3,000 bridges and 67 tunnels to allow a clear and largely straight path, led to such huge cost overruns that, even though the project was financed by the government and had additional funding from the World Bank that Mr Shima has secured himself, he resigned in 1963 in the Japanese tradition of taking responsibility, along with the JNR president Shinji Sogō, who had backed Shima's ideas, even though the line later proved to be popular and well-used. They both did not attend the opening ceremony.

Further reading: 

[list]
[*] [url=https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9B%BD%E9%89%84C52%E5%BD%A2%E8%92%B8%E6%B0%97%E6%A9%9F%E9%96%A2%E8%BB%8A]familiarize yourself with the JNR C52's history[/url]
[*] [url=https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9B%BD%E9%89%84C53%E5%BD%A2%E8%92%B8%E6%B0%97%E6%A9%9F%E9%96%A2%E8%BB%8A#]do the same about the C53[/url]
[*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gresley_conjugated_valve_gear]there's also a fine article about the Gresley-Holcroft gear[/url]
[*] [url=http://steam.fan.coocan.jp/engines/C53.htm]take a look at schematics comparing streamlined C53 and a baseline C53 locomotive[/url]
[*] read more on[url=https://www.oldtokyo.com/j-g-r-j-n-r-steam-locomotive-evolution-1872-1948/] JGR/JNR Steam Locomotive Evolution from 1872 to 1948[/url]
[*] go through the rest of the translated portion of[url=https://www.ejrcf.or.jp/jrtr/jrtr03/f45_shi.html] Birth of The Shinkansen— A Memoir by Hideo Shima[/url]
[*] find out more about[url=https://www.ejrcf.or.jp/jrtr/jrtr27/pdf/f40_ina.pdf] JNR's transition from steam power to EMUs[/url]
[*] and here is an article about [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinkansen]the Shinkansen of course[/url]


[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/e6153410652b85306f7e9f8fa318f80218cc37f5.png[/img]

Hello friends! Due to the fact that many people had to stay at home in isolation due to COVID-19, we decided to add another Let's Play Together competition in the middle of the week, just for fun-with different crazy levels and (alas!) no prizes. We think it is clear by now this extra LPT is a permanent addition too :)

The rules are the same: log in to our Discord server, keep it running, play a competitive level, complete it with 5 stars and have fun! 
Visit our [url=https://discord.gg/train-valley]Discord server[/url] (#lets-play-together channel) to learn more.

This week's level is 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3417415793

Just open the game - there's a link right on the main menu screen.

Good luck everyone!

notes.title: Let's Play Together - The Cows Are in Charge
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/e30265846dbe0f91cf1a1f6ca0212f9cf306cca7.png[/img]

Hello friends! Every Friday 17:30 UTC/GMT - we hold a “Let’s play together” competition. During next 24 hours everyone is welcome to try and score the best time in a preselected level. Join our Discord server and keep Discord running while playing — your results will be automatically published in the #lets-play-together channel. [u]You need to get 5 stars to qualify.[/u]

Glittering prizes include:
1) Top 3 winners receive one random card each. Collect 18 locomotive cards and advance to next set of 8 all new cards! Complete that second set and enter a final tier of 12 rare cards! Assemble all cards from all tiers and receive a special prize. Easy!
2) Every player registered by our Discord bot has a chance to get a card. The number of cards depends on the number of participants: one additional card for every 10 train connoisseurs on the list. More players means more prizes!
2.5) One non-Champion from the top 10 gets a Challenger Card - introduced along with 12 new loco cards from Myths And Rails and Editor's Bulletin!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/da8f894851a5b1d8e435fac676c6a5309d381e2b.jpg[/img]

Visit our [url=https://discord.gg/train-valley]Discord server[/url] (#lets-play-together channel) to learn more.

A level we are playing this week is 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3412482713

Now open your game - the link is right there in the main menu.

Good luck everyone!

notes.title: Happy Holidays! ☃️
notes.notes:
🎄Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year! 🎁

[previewyoutube=Hzn7apSYrUw;full][/previewyoutube]

We are very grateful that you continue driving trains together with us all this time 🚂 As you're reading this, we are preparing the next announcement in the Train Valley series 😰, but for now we want you, our player, to have the best Christmas holidays among your favorite people, enjoying your favorite treats and sharing your favorite festive activities.
Let the feeling of warmth, joy, and care stay with you throughout the holidays and the next year. See you in 2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣5️⃣!

notes.title: Patent Pending DLC Level Design Contest Results
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/b0d326d1ed6eaae391bb39fe8228ab11acf1ae85.png[/img]

Hello there! The final round of Patent Pending level design contest results is up, time to announce our winners:

[h1]1st place: :tv2conductor: Eijolend - :tvloco: Spider Cafe[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3229825692
[i]10:30, SOFLTO, stop the timers with an Inhibitor for 210 seconds.[/i]

Yet another train valley set in @Eijolend's Arachnidverse 🙂 Continuing the trend of eightlegged cooperation, friendly alchemist spiders living nearby host free tasting sessions of their newest concoction - hot chocolate so good it feels like time stops while you are drinking it (patent pending). Stop by the Spider Cafe, get a steaming mug and watch our shiny Adiunkts do all the work. For spiders crave Cyber Crystals and don't allow chocolate drinks outside their nest... 🤔

[h1]2nd place: :tv2conductor: Thomas - :tvloco: Hot drink and cheesecake 2[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3223491876
[i]12 minutes, keep an industry sped up with a Catalyst for 60 seconds, travel 500 tiles while an Inhibitor is working. [/i]

What does one get by combining Magnets, Cheese and moderate amounts of time dilation? An engaging train puzzle valley with quite a bit of planning and just enough time for your plans' execution. Spend your Magnets wisely, don't go chasing every bridge construction site and watch your hot drink of choice supplies 🙂
Indeed, thank you @Blathers for the Warehouse idea! 🙂

[h1]3rd place: :tv2conductor: LittleBear - :tvloco: Hot Chocolate and Soup[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3219021701
[i]12 minutes, no wrong deliveries, keep an industry sped up with a Catalyst for 200 seconds.[/i]

And here we have our first recipe of Spider soup 🙂 Can be fed into a Catalyst as fuel, traded as a commodity for some hot chocolate, used to fill in old mining sites or just enjoyed during a long haul over the snowy plains of Hot Chocolate and Soup. Keep the trade going, industries sped up and Adiunkts running! 🙂

[h1]:tvhook: Bonus award nomination #1 - A new contestant: :tv2conductor: ManaFriendsmith - :tvloco: Lock and Load[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3235630499
[i]15 minutes, SOFLTO, keep an industry sped up with a Catalyst for 240 seconds.[/i]

We have only 15 minutes before they flood the canal. And even though we can bribe the canal authorities with fuel to extend that time, other things require our immediate attention. Locomotive upgrades, Incremental Toll Station construction and following fees, keeping both Inhibitor and Catalyst in check, getting those Appliances to the other side - Lock and Load is a complex endeavor and a very satisfying puzzle to solve 🙂

[h1]:tvhook: Bonus award nomination #2 - Back from the Workshop: :tv2conductor: brunocharles - :tvloco: Around the motorway[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3222156427
[i]11 minutes, DNSAT, travel 1000 tiles while an Inhibitor is working.[/i]

Terraforming, time freezing, not stopping trains (combined with fastest locomotives TV2 can offer)! So many things can go wrong, but luckily we have access to a Paperclip factory, and there's nothing you can't fix with some paperclips - pollution, itchy bears or even excessive clock elasticity 🙂 Tame the Electric Motors autotrain and make your deliveries, or pay in Gold ore to delay your inevitable win 🙂

notes.title: Train Valley 2 is 5 years old!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/88dee87dfbd63c6818a2443e436f3c7525885cfb.png[/img]

On April 15, 2019 Train Valley 2 was released on Steam.

First Pioneers left the depot on Forestry and our quest for fast and precise cargo deliveries began. Choo-Choo Weekly issues followed to commemorate your first expeditions into the depths of the level Editor, and Let's Play Together! challenges became our good old tradition in the blink of an eye :)

A trove of additional content, thousands of Workshop uploads and hundreds of LPT challenges, releases on additional platforms and screens upon screens filled with your feedback, suggestions, questions and answers and reports about your improved timing and screenshots of that bridge bug-soon-to-be-feature Train Valley 2 have evolved, its community have grown, and our firm belief that making games is about making sure people enjoy them stayed.

Thank you for believing in us and our games, supporting us every step of the way and showing us good fun with the way you drive your trains, discover undocumented behaviors, or just discuss the best way to measure the speed of a locomotive leaving a Depot in tiles per millisecond. You are what makes Train Valley 2 so wonderful :) 

See you in a bit, friends!

Hello there!

[b]Patent Pending[/b] is out, and we hope you are enjoying new level objectives, industries, stations, goods and resource types you have encountered while chasing the escaped Catalyst prototype.
 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2848820/Train_Valley_2__Patent_Pending/

We are hosting a dedicated level design contest [b]from 1 April to 1 May of 2024[/b]. Any completable level using new gameplay additions can enter and win a prize - one out of five.

:tvhook: [b]The rules: [/b] :tvhook:

Use any of the following:
[list]
[*] :tvvagon: [b]Increasing Toll[/b] station,
[*] :tvvagon: [b]Catalyst[/b] and
[*] :tvvagon: [b]Inhibitor[/b] industries as well as

[*] :tvloco: [b]Stop the level's timer with an Inhibitor for XX seconds[/b],
[*] :tvloco: [b]Pay XX TV2$ at an Increasing Toll Station[/b],
[*] :tvloco: [b]Travel XX tiles while an Inhibitor is working[/b] objectives.

You [b]don't have to[/b] use every new station and industry type in a single level to make it eligible (although you definitely can :) Any [b]1 station/industry[/b] or [b]1 objective is enough[/b]. Feel free to sprinkle your creation on top with some new decorations too :)

notes.title: Locomotive 3-8 (The Doctor)
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/0f4edc065832c99e36ae9479bfc6a25e42804b07.jpg[/img] (SPMW 207 at Donner Pass, 2017 - photo by Mike Haire from [url=http://www.rrpicturearchives.net/showPicture.aspx?id=4660499]Railroad Picture Archives[/url])

The North America Railway Hall of Fame recognizes and establishes an enduring tribute to the people and things that have made significant contribution relating to the railway industry in North America - and our today's locomotive/railroad equipment is so effective it[url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140508034151/http://narhf.org/?p=5671] was inducted in 2001 into the "Technical Innovations" category with "National" significance. [/url]

[h2]Forgotten, but not obsolete.[/h2]

Solid steel plows, snow throwers, flangers, snow melters, snow blowers powered by jet engines all exist and some are deployed every winter across the globe, yet the rotary snowplows still outperform the competition in both power-to-efficiency and spectacular snow removal nominations.

Several reasons for the forgotten part: advent of more ubiquitous service and construction vehicles like bulldozers and the sheer maintenance cost of a single unit - even if it isn't actively used, just stored. 

Of course there are disadvantages too.
[list]
[*] Rotary snowplows are more susceptible to debris (rocks, trees, etc.) found in the snow slides resulting from avalanches. 
[*] Rotaries leave an open-cut that fixed-blade plows cannot push snow past, and so once rotaries have been used, they must be used for the remainder of the season, until the snowpack - multiple layers of compacted snow - has melted. Often deployed when snow is too deep or hard-packed for traditional plows though, the rotary's ability to operate slowly, as there is no requirement for train momentum to break up the snow, is often an advantage in mountainous regions, where a high speed derailment could be disastrous.
[*] Rotaries are also less used on routes with axle load restriction - with a weaker bridge along the way for example.
[/list]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RjBQ3MaBYiU
[url=https://www.youtube.com/@jakemiillephotography]Video by Jake Miille Photography[/url]

Today these magnificent machines are used as a last resort, when less expensive fixed-blades are overwhelmed by especially large snow quantities, mainly around mountain passes and areas with poor road access, or areas with routine severe snowfall conditions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/0e1d985c3abf752a49342050d54c1afbe68fd65c.jpg[/img](SPMW 207 at Donner Pass, 2017 - photo by Mike Haire from [url=http://www.rrpicturearchives.net/showPicture.aspx?id=4660508]Railroad Picture Archives[/url])
[b][i]Notice the fold out "wings" on both sides of the blade assembly that allow the plow to grab more snow and clean a wider area.[/i][/b]

Train Valley 2’s in-game counterpart is called The Doctor because the initial rotary snowplow design was proposed by J.W. Elliot, a Canadian dentist in 1869. 

He never got to building one; first working models of that same design were tested with sand by one Orange Jull of Orangeville, Ontario and later developed into a successful full-sized working prototype in cooperation with Leslie Brothers of Toronto that owned a machine shop there. Around a year later, Leslies acquired the rights, formed the Rotary Steam Shovel Manufacturing Company in Paterson, New Jersey and contracted Cooke Locomotive and Machine Works in Paterson to do the actual construction. 

A Leslie Plow is the type of plow most people think of when you say "rotary". It has one large circular plow blade rotating on a shaft that is parallel to the tracks. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/9cefd7732f4fabf577e0b15683d056c377c9b522.jpg[/img]
(Steam rotary snowplow OM, built in 1889 by Cooke Locomotive & Machine Works, preserved today on the Cumbres & Toltec Scenic Railroad. - photo by Benoit Poulin, 2002, from [url=http://drgw.free.fr/DRGW/MOW/Snow/Rotary/CTS-02-261_en.htm]American Steam and Narrow Gauge website[/url])

Between 1885 and 1903 the Leslies had 62 plows (plus 2 for export) built by several locomotive works.  They then sold the rights to the American Locomotive Company (ALCo), however, the Leslies' company exists to this day. From 1905 to
1937 ALCo built 67 plows (plus 4 for export), and oversaw construction of several more by Reid Newfoundland and Lima-Hamilton before going out of business in 1969.

There were other designs of course, some more successful than others, but that's a tale for another time perchance? :)

[h2]The most powerful piece of snowfighting equipment ever devised[/h2]

Our inspiration came from the units SPMW 207 and SPMW 209 assigned to Union Pacific Railroad's Roseville Subdivision, California - both Leslie Rotary Plows, they were originally built with steam power and rebuilt during the 1950s to power the blade assembly by diesel locomotive traction motors. Today they are regularly sent out to move the "Sierra Cement" snow found on the Donner Pass Line. 

They get their electrical power from separate EMD F7B units, that were repurposed to power the rotaries, and themselves don't have traction motors. The F7B units are known as "snails" (this is derived from the fact that engineless but motored units that take their power from another locomotive are "slugs"; thus the opposite, with engine but no motors, is a "snail.")
These plows are equipped with a Vapor-Clarkson steam generator too - handy for heat, cleaning ice out of the wheel and off the antennas, as well as blowing the steam whistle :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/485ed7efe6f75016b590d2199cd48ead61b70963.jpg[/img](SPMW 207 at at Colfax Railroad days, 2014 - photo by Mike Haire from [url=http://www.rrpicturearchives.net/showPicture.aspx?id=3985666]Railroad Picture Archives[/url])

The blade assembly can rotate in either direction, while the blades automatically position themselves to the proper angle, and the chute can be quickly switched to throw the snow to either side. The rotaries' trucks are rigid to help prevent derailments and keep the blades at a constant height. The rotaries are also chained to their respective 'snail'. Neither the rotary nor the snail can move by themselves, and rely totally on attendant locomotives to pull or push them. 

Normally, the rotary plows are placed on either end of a train, which would consist of a plow, snail, three or four locomotives that provide tractive power, another snail and a rotary facing in the opposite direction. This was done so that the train would not be trapped in case of a slide or additional snowfall behind it, and the train would not need to be turned. UP's SPMW units are equipped with controls that allow handling every aspect of a train like that - movement, heat, power - from the plow's cabin.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/71b0dfb0cb3bcf4cac09f2c9572880e0e0185856.png[/img]

Observe the Doctor's signature circular blade assembly encased in fire engine red armor in the front, along with a leftside chute and a bulky, Train Valley 2 yellow car body equipped with longer access ladders containing the crew compartment, several observation windows and housing both diesel traction motors and the rotary engine (a necessary simplification stemming from the way locomotives work in Train Valley 2), with a bright orange warning light on the roof. A projection of power and reliability - qualities needed the most for the tasks ahead.

And that is it for today!
For a bit of further reading you [url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090214181543/http://n6ecv.net/Rotarys.html]you can take a peek inside a UP rotary plow - a walkthrough by Jim R. Ley[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hbLyXtzLX3I]watch a steam rotary snowplow train in action - filmed by Mike Armstrong.[/url]

See you in a bit, friends!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/6418c926b270a11b974fa566a9cd11324ac587fc.png[/img]

Hello friends! Every Friday 17:30 UTC/GMT - we hold a “Let’s play together” competition. During next 24 hours everyone is welcome to try and score the best time in a preselected level. Join our Discord server and keep Discord running while playing — your results will be automatically published in the #lets-play-together channel. [u]You need to get 5 stars to qualify.[/u]

Glittering prizes include:
1) Top 3 winners receive one random card each. Collect 18 locomotive cards and advance to next set of 8 all new cards! Complete that second set and enter a final tier of 12 rare cards! Assemble all cards from all tiers and receive a special prize. Easy!
2) Every player registered by our Discord bot has a chance to get a card. The number of cards depends on the number of participants: one additional card for every 10 train connoisseurs on the list. More players means more prizes!
2.5) One non-Champion from the top 10 gets a Challenger Card - introduced along with 12 new loco cards from Myths And Rails and Editor's Bulletin!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/da8f894851a5b1d8e435fac676c6a5309d381e2b.jpg[/img]

Visit our [url=https://discord.gg/train-valley]Discord server[/url] (#lets-play-together channel) to learn more.

A level we are playing this week is 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3146081182

Now open your game - the link is right there in the main menu.

Good luck everyone!

notes.title: Happy New Year!
notes.notes:
As we were preparing this Friday's LPT challenge to celebrate another year of Train Valley 2 coming to a close, we took a minute to thank you for your interest in our games, your support and feedback, tireless exploration efforts for new Workshop designs and meticulous research into undocumented train behaviors :)

Check out these stats and see what we've accomplished together in 2023:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/cc214207606b8f0d975dfd091abe36f02134f7d2.png[/img]

Here's to mastering all the LPT applications for the Locosaurus, stacking 10 terraforming markers into the same terrain tile, overcoming DNRT and DNUP and DNSAT, choosing the scout bot before the loot and after that getting the loot anyway, wondering what does a Mechacow milk Cheesecake taste like, combining Worker stations with bridges and not being prepared for the unforeseen consequences, completing just one more train puzzle...or maybe three :)

Flazm Interactive team wishes you happy holidays. See you in 2024!

----

*Do Not Reverse Trains
*Do Not Use Pause
*Do Not Stop Any Trains

----

notes.title: Get your Railway Puzzles Bundle today
notes.notes:
We’ve once again teamed up with our friends and fellow train puzzles connoisseurs at [b]Afterburn[/b] and [b]Galaxy Grove[/b] to offer the [b]Railway Puzzles Bundle[/b] - with the maximum discount ever!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/6ce0063561dd81c17998f72bf148e8f2bdeb0060.jpg[/img]

A minimalistic voxel-art game by [b]Galaxy Grove[/b], [b]Station To Station[/b] is about bringing colour, life and relaxation to the world around you through the magic of trains. Build railway connections, stitch sun-kissed dunes and emerald woods together - for every station has a tale to tell.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/35369/Railway_Puzzles_Bundle/

We have invited aboard [b]Afterburn[/b] for that bundle too. They are the makers of [b]Railbound[/b], a comfy, relaxing railway track-bending puzzle game about a pair of dogs on a journey around the world. Connect and sever rails, help everyone reach their homes, pick up your friends on the way and make the train go 'CHOO-CHOO' :)

This bundle includes [b]Station to Station[/b], [b]Railbound[/b], [b]Train Valley[/b], and [b]Train Valley 2[/b]. Players purchasing this bundle will receive an even greater, worthy of Steam Winter Sale discount across all 4 titles. And if you already own a title within the bundle then you can purchase the others at a further discounted rate, so do not hesitate - there can never be too many train puzzles :)

See you in a bit, friends!

notes.title: Train Valley 2: Community Edition is now available

Hello there!

We - Flazm Interactive in cooperation with Blitworks Games - are happy to announce that [b]Train Valley 2: Community Edition[/b] is out now for Nintendo Switch, Xbox One and PlayStation 4 - a familiar blend of puzzles, trains and advanced calculus that can now be experienced with your gaming system of choice:

[url=https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/train-valley-2-community-edition-switch/]https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/train-valley-2-community-edition-switch/[/url]
[url=https://www.xbox.com/en-us/games/store/train-valley-2-community-edition/9nhs6134h27z]https://www.xbox.com/en-us/games/store/train-valley-2-community-edition/9nhs6134h27z[/url]
[url=https://store.playstation.com/en-us/concept/10004915]https://store.playstation.com/en-us/concept/10004915[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/01a36607ff6a78130423f6aa05a4490bc3705678.jpg[/img]

And be sure to check out [b]Train Valley Collection Deluxe Edition[/b] made possible by our friends at Numskull Games that includes both Train Valley 1 + Train Valley 2 with added DLCs as well as a [b]3D papercraft train station diorama[/b] and a [b]4-piece train set with a diecast locomotive[/b] - available from your local retailer. Push the purple Order Now button to find out more:

[url=https://numskullgames.com/game/train-valley-collection/]https://numskullgames.com/game/train-valley-collection/[/url]

See you in a bit, friends!

notes.title: Please vote for Train Valley games in the Steam Awards!
notes.notes:
Hello there!

Countless cargo deliveries later we are looking back on all these years of DLCs, LPTs, DNUPs, DNSATs, locomotives length per-pixel spreadsheet calculations - and closing in on uncountable quantities of railway switches operated - the foundations of what Train Valley is today thanks to our community's support and feedback.
And then we look forward, to new train puzzles heights before us, for we are not quite done yet :)

If you feel like it, we’d be honored to get your nomination for the “Labor of Love” category in this year’s Steam Awards.

And stay tuned for future announcements by joining our Discord at [url=https://discord.com/invite/train-valley] https://discord.com/invite/train-valley [/url]

See you in a bit, friends!
-Flazm Interactive team

notes.title: Level of the Month - June and July 2023
notes.notes:
June and July of 2023 seem to be just on the last page of your calendar, and yet September is almost over. Shall we replay two most prominent summer train puzzles and reminisce hot sunny days and hotter 5-star timers?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/60f856483434db20f19599121b12438cda029dae.png[/img]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2993228916

Now with electricity! :)
Several updates later, after closely working with the community, an upgraded, higher difficulty valley emerged. Supplying the megapolis with materials, bridging the central island with the banks, investing in new factories, incorporating existing track branches into the ever-growing railway network, looking out for shortcuts, keeping your eye on every delivery - Mountain's River is and exhilarating kind of  'drive your trains straight into a puzzle' fun. 
[i]45:00, no train crashing or wrong deliveries.[/i]

A very good result for a second Workshop map ever uploaded. Congratulations @hugoleger91 - your €30 Steam gift card should've found its way to you not too long ago!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/961711ed9a1e13b8627e6922c8e26abcd00e3374.png[/img]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3008946195

[i]Arrrabbiiian niiiiights....[/i] "One of them maps", according to our players, took the cake in July - and took our LPT veterans for a ride as well :) Dune elves, forgotten treasures, a majestic desert city surrounded by oases with quite a few delivery quests - a good place to make a coin, maybe haggle a little too - and no room for stopping your trains in the scorching sands, keeping onto your Cheese for too long or crossing the Sultan by crashing their precious locomotives. 
[i]16:00, DNSAT, no train crashing.[/i]

Congratulations @Gaztibelza - we've made sure your €30 award is already with you :)

Train Valley 2 community and developers want you, reader, to bring out your level editor and show us train driving complexity levels we never knew even existed. Build, create, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/1640912759106326420/]compete[/url]. Having fun is a requirement :)

See you in a bit, friends!

notes.title: The Railway Puzzles Bundle is now available
notes.notes:
We’re excited to announce that we’re teaming up with our friends and fellow train puzzles connoisseurs at [b]Afterburn[/b] and [b]Galaxy Grove[/b] to offer the [b]Railway Puzzles Bundle[/b] in support of the just released [b]Station To Station[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/6ce0063561dd81c17998f72bf148e8f2bdeb0060.jpg[/img]

A minimalistic voxel-art game by [b]Galaxy Grove[/b], [b]Station To Station[/b] is about bringing colour, life and relaxation to the world around you through the magic of trains. Build railway connections, stitch sun-kissed dunes and emerald woods together - for every station has a tale to tell.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/35369/Railway_Puzzles_Bundle/

We have invited aboard [b]Afterburn[/b] for that bundle too. They are the makers of [b]Railbound[/b], a comfy, relaxing railway track-bending puzzle game about a pair of dogs on a journey around the world. Connect and sever rails, help everyone reach their homes, pick up your friends on the way and make the train go 'CHOO-CHOO' :)

This bundle includes [b]Station to Station[/b], [b]Railbound[/b], [b]Train Valley[/b], and [b]Train Valley 2[/b]. Players purchasing this bundle will receive a discount across all 4 titles. And if you already own a title within the bundle then you can purchase the others at a further discounted rate, so do not hesitate - there can never be too many train puzzles :)

See you in a bit, friends!

notes.title: Level of the Month - April and May 2023
notes.notes:
April and May of 2023 have gone by - but there's two tales of large scale freights deliveries, industrial grade train puzzles and multilevel bridge-it-till-you're-broke Passenger Flow valleys to remember them by:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/c3842e9218fb8c7637df07f5f33118bc3f945e69.png[/img]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2963476208
The locals are really fond of their mines, so much so they've settled right next to a freshly collapsed one - not ceasing their business for a second. Take special precautions while constructing your bridges - expensive as they are, and PF trains having little patience + One Way Stations restricting all movement on the lower level, and massive Pumpkin industrial complex requiring immediate attention above, there's always a restart waiting close by :)
[i]12:30, DNDATT, DNRT.[/i]

Excellent design, high replayability and fun gameplay. Congratulations @Plastickbag - your €30 Steam gift card should've found its way to you not too long ago!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/5c4e7ea015c602d13d8b79bb4e7a425e2234b64f.png[/img]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2979020369

A miniature shunting yard with shiny blue steam engines - welcome to Switchback Summit where getting from point A to point B usually requires rerouting via F :) Pay attention to every switch, remember the 15 000 TV2$ fee on that Toll Station and work along/around local terrain peculiarities, guide your trains over the narrow mountain tracks and complete your delivery quests on time.
[spoiler]Yes, it is possible to reverse trains without failing the Do Not Reverse Trains condition :)[/spoiler]
[i]14:00, DNRT, no engine upgrades allowed.[/i]

A refreshing design hidden beneath a classic layout. Congratulations @Yokuyin - we've made sure your €30 award is already with you :)

Train Valley 2 community and developers want you, reader, to bring out your level editor and show us train driving complexity levels we never knew even existed. Build, create, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/1640912759106326420/]compete[/url]. Having fun is a requirement :)

See you in a bit, friends!

notes.title: Level of the Month - February and March 2023
notes.notes:
Level of the Month February and March 2023 edition is here - two tales of fast deliveries, completed objectives and closely watched timers, both getting our highest commendations. Take your pick:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/c5da1b71ed185d6aba63ec61a1bb807987f38ec4.png[/img]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2933104639

Our resident Spider Chocolatier presents us another peak into the intricacies of human-arachnid relations, specifically the Arachnoenergetic industry. An ancient 50000 Spiderwatts-class ritual stopped working and now energy-less valley seeks to restore an old Powerplant. A selection of differently themed Editor assets blending into a complete story also turns out to be a puzzle with unique flow to its gameplay, possessing both multitasking exercises, tactical financial decisions to make and good bit of junction (re)building too. 
[i]19:00, no train crashes, 20000 TV2$ demolition budget.[/i]

Excellent design, high replayability and fun gameplay. Congratulations @eijolend - your €30 Steam gift card should've found its way to you not too long ago!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/c7a8632e56f9621235873ee1d93bcafbc891ab1f.png[/img]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2949657520
The story and the valley's name feel oddly familiar, yet the inner workings of the local supply chain do not. Powerful multitasking capabilities, an interesting Engineer distribution minigame, a piece of terrain floating in the black wastness of space design - Attack Of The Clones is an excellent example of "fun landscaping meets a fresh strategy" kind of valley. Adding no loco upgrades and limited funds into the mix, we get a refreshing experience of exploring new tricks of our favorite train driving game. Hope you like sand :)
[i]15:00, build at least 2 bridges and 1 tunnel.[/i]

Congratulations @hika - we've made sure your €30 award is already with you :)

notes.title: The Pandeia Project Level Design Contest Results Are In!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/6bfda215e77c61cfbbd240086cd198e4d4e4025d.png[/img]

Hello! The fifth, final round of instantaneously assessed and unanimously selected level(s) exploring new additions from our latest DLC Workshop creator(s) have presented for the past 4 days is here:

[h2]1st place: :tv2conductor: Plastickbag - :tvloco: Lazy Cheesecake[/h2]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3028160639

Congratulations Plastickbag, your €10 Steam gift card is on its way to you. And now on to the final contest results:

[h1]1st place: :tv2conductor: Plastickbag - :tvloco: Lazy Cheesecake[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3028160639
[i]19 minutes, don't buy more than 2 engines and produce at least 350 units.[/i]

There's nothing like praising a level twice in the same post - especially since it brings so much to one's play session. All the eligibility conditions aside, Lazy Cheesecake teaches us two different cheesecake recipes, helps keeping our multitasking/time management/track planning in top shape and offers a whole new type of a level layout - one that implements Accelerators as time constraining devices while utilizing Linked Gates as bullet points in your shopping list - and that leads us to excellent replayability backed up by possible supply chain shortcuts and our PPLDC's first place!

[h1]2nd place: :tv2conductor: hika - :tvloco: Castle in the Sky[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3023977402
[i]18 minutes, SOFLTO, build at least 1 bridge. [/i]

A train puzzle to prove that timely deliveries and expertly operated Passenger Flow trains are equally important wherever your transportation company finds itself next - like a floating island for example :)
Keeping up with unexplained recent increase in popularity of Cheese and Robots and Protective Suits, your mission is to meet local demand with appropriate, efficient and precise levels of supply - just watch that autotrain and don't look over the edge too much :)

[h1]3rd place: :tv2conductor: BenGotham - :tvloco: The Teddy Bears' Picnic[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3013426142
[i]SOFLTO, no wrong deliveries, 16 minutes.[/i]

Let's help teddies make some tasty treats, sew some new friends and have a wonderful picnic together! The operation's overseer prefers trainspotting fully loaded trains while the harbormaster is inspecting every freight and does not allow more that one train through the gates, so let's indulge them too. Complete the railway junction around the middle city and see the preparations completed just in time to start the festivities. Don't let the bees sting your Navigators :)

Our heartiest congratulations go to our winners! Playing your creations fueled by recently added mechanics and industries is as fun as it is insightful - and Train Valley 2 is steaming towards more changes and new content thanks to your feedback and unyielding interest in making sure every delivery is headed to where it is needed most. Our thank you goes to every level uploader, puzzle solver and train driver that keep Train Valley 2 Workshop going! 

See you in a bit, friends!

notes.title: Announcing Train Valley World, Arriving in 2024!
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/2iPg2D2.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Flazm Interactive[/b], in cooperation with [b]tinyBuild[/b], is proud to present the next [i][b]Train Valley[/b][/i] game that will bring our players back to the height of the Second Industrial Revolution in the 1900s.[/h3]

Travel around the globe across 25 levels inspired by real-life locations like London, Las Vegas, Cairo, Athens, Frankfurt, and Paris. Make timely deliveries, witness historical events, and help discover, invent, and build the foundations of modern civilization. Welcome to [i][b]Train Valley Word[/b][/i]!

[h3][b]WISHLIST NOW:[/b][/h3]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2244470/Train_Valley_World/

[b]FEATURES[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]New railroad tycoon gameplay mechanics:[/b] geared up with railroad automation, intellectual train scheduling, free placement industry building, ability to connect several depots to a single production, and assignable locomotive perks our players will be able to construct complex logistical systems and support multibranch supply chains. 
[*] [b]Different challenges:[/b] limited starting resources, optional objectives, and delivery quests hierarchy will introduce additional challenge—both for a chance to earn additional funds, to test one’s multitasking skills, and as a storytelling device. 
[*] [b]Improved level editor:[/b] new scripting tools, programmable scenarios, evolving cities, reactive dynamic water, day/night cycle, thousands of new placeable objects, and numerous quality-of-life improvements. 
[*] [b]Online multiplayer:[/b] for the first time in the Train Valley franchise, multiplayer for up to 4 players will be available from launch. Face the level’s challenges, devise a railroad system by building around existing tracks, and establish logistical and financial dominance while sharing produced resources.
[/list]

[h3]Watch the announcement trailer:[/h3]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8afdaQKRdSw

[i][b]Train Valley World[/b][/i] is scheduled to arrive on Steam [b]in 2024[/b].
To learn more, visit the [url=http://trainvalley.world/]game’s website[/url], follow [url=https://twitter.com/trainvalley]@TrainValley[/url] on Twitter, [url=https://www.facebook.com/trainvalley/]connect with us on Facebook[/url], join the [url=https://discord.com/invite/train-valley]official Discord[/url], and add [i][b]Train Valley World[/b][/i] to your wishlist today!

notes.title: Editor's Bulletin is out!
notes.notes:
Hello there!

High stakes, powerful locomotives and complex equations that will make your calculator smoke. Wiggly tracks, THE spreadsheet with engine model's length, hidden (?) achievements, shiny new cards fresh off the press.

Let's get right down to business: Train Valley 2 - Editor's Bulletin is now available :)

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2330180/Train_Valley_2__Editors_Bulletin/

[list]
[*] 30 new valleys
[*] 6 new locomotives
[*] Locomotive preview mode
[*] GEM packs stars swapped for shiny Gems + now there's even more Stars to earn along with...
[*] ...right you are - new achievements, including both Gems and Stars points systems :)
[*] Let's Play Together award system overhauled and expanded with new collectibles
[*] Various bug fixes
[/list]

Please enjoy the launch day discount - available through April 19th - and tell us what you think here in the comments and join our Discord at [url=https://discord.com/invite/train-valley] https://discord.com/invite/train-valley[/url] to keep up to date with the latest Train Valley #news [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/3148519094655067065/]and weekly challenges.[/url]

See you in a bit, friends! 

:tv2computer: [url=https://twitter.com/TrainValley]Our Twitter[/url].

notes.title: Now approaching: Editor's Bulletin
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

A high-stakes business of driving freight trains to anywhere our engineers can lay some rails to relies on timely reports as much as it does on fast and powerful locomotives. Editor's Bulletin is almost here bringing you case studies on building and maintaining supply chains entirely with wiggly tracks, crucial stats on locomotive and tender model's length (now down to 10 digits after decimal point!) and a centerfold housing the updated chart on star-timer's fairness, hidden (?) achievements count and number of Potato Power Plants present correlation.     
[b]Wishlist today![/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2330180/Train_Valley_2__Editors_Bulletin/

High stakes — and high rewards too: we're updating our LPT collectible prize pool with [b]12 new cards[/b] depicting your favorite engines from Myths And Rails and Editor's Bulletin. All current Champions will have a chance of competing side by side with current contenders and complete their collections again :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/bcd94f980a705a2f3d4fbebba37fa16fab767f49.png[/img]

As always, we will be waiting for your feedback. And will be waiting for you to join our Discord - in case you want to have all the latest Train Valley news at your fingertips :)

See you in a bit, friends!

notes.title: Level of the Month - January 2023
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/3c7e7c52cdbdf80c53544a6509f538105bc31c55.png[/img]

The energy crisis is nigh here and even though we have several options the timers work not in our favour - not to mention the particularities of local logistics and the DNSAT. We are here to avert Electricity Shortage 1:

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2910931949

The Potato Power Plant is on standby but we have to put in quite some work before utilizing its full potential. Topographical layout and 9:20 timer aside, simultaneous laying down tracks and counting your Workers output add a multitasking challenge to candle making, potion brewing, puzzling valley we have selected for Level Of The Month' January 2023. [spoiler]Don't spend too much time trying to connect that Wind Turbine Powerplant please :) [/spoiler]

Peculiar design, solid replayability and fun gameplay. Congratulations @petronille_marie - your €30 Steam gift card is well on its way!

Train Valley 2 community and developers want you, reader, to bring out your level editor and show us train driving complexity levels we never knew even existed. Build, create, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/1640912759106326420/]compete[/url]. Having fun is a requirement :)

notes.title: Level of the Year 2022
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/1cd919c9b55a1a6d1706072cf7b078c42018584a.png[/img]

Nearly 500 Workshop levels and 96 Let's Play Together challenges later (check out full 2022 infographics here by the way) https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/602320/view/3641754849917112134 the time has come to choose a level worthy of the [b]Level Of The Year 2022[/b] award.
New Editor objects, new gameplay mechanics, new locomotives to drive, new levels to explore-we brought a little a bit of everything to enrich and maximize your Train Valley 2 experience, all of it based on your feedback, suggestions and questions. Flazm Interactive would like to express gratitude to every Train Valley player. We are very glad to have you.

Reconnect the settlements of this river valley, supply local industrial and agricultural businesses, expand your railway network, be on the lookout for many ways to improve your schedule and streamline your deliveries, maintain that 65 000 TV2$ demolition jobs cost limit, do not crash any trains and practice some more your last second route switching. 

We hope you enjoy your visit to the

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2819697388

With 10 minutes on that Pass Limiter's cooldown timer and 16 on the 5-star one this puzzle can still be solved-in time-by utilizing several different approaches in both resource distribution and engine management. Not every shortcut can be built during a single playthrough though, so some early planning seems to be a viable strategy too. A lively, compact and fun to explore valley offering solution variability resulting in additional restarts-just to see if there's a better way to design everything-while catering to different skill levels. 

@Gatebase, outstanding work! A €50 Steam gift card is heading your way right now.

Train Valley 2 community and developers want you, reader, to bring out your level editor and show us train driving complexity levels we never knew even existed. Build, create, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/1640912759106326420/]compete[/url]. Having fun is a requirement :)

notes.title: Level of the Month - October/December 2022
notes.notes:
Level of the Month October and December 2022 edition is here-two tales of fast deliveries, completed objectives and closely watched timers, both getting our highest commendations. Take your pick:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/eb842c618759a1205bf43209576a97404b248d71.png[/img]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2876088539

A certain space station/planet destroyer reimagined within TV2 Editor with hidden terraforming events, autotrains, DNDATT fused into a puzzle worth finest train drivers rebellion has. Ignore your onboard targeting computer malfunctioning and deliver explosive payloads, disable the station's turrets and save the day in under 10 minutes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/8e44435b8506f9e3ec310fc066f1806189b94477.png[/img]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2900817613

The future is now, and instead of flying cars we have got flying trains (patent pending :) Current prototypes can go up to 7 tiles without any tracks - or land - beneath. Using that cutting edge tech we're tasked to retrieve an ultra rare cyber crystal right from the core of a futuristic settlement on the other side of the chasm. DNRT, 12:00, sneaky terraforming and a sloooow Pass Limiter.

Excellent designs with similarly high replayability and fun gameplay. Congratulations @Blathers, @Miaxlo-your €30 Steam gift cards are on the way!

Train Valley 2 community and developers want you, reader, to bring out your level editor and show us train driving complexity levels we never knew even existed. Check out these impressive stats and see what we've accomplished together in 2022:

Here is to overcoming DNRT and DNUP, finding and selling overpriced scenery objects to fund an extra bridge construction, perfecting your Spider chocolate recipe, building a wiggly track section around reloading Pass Limiters, powering an entire valley with a Potato Power Plant, disassembling Alien Artifacts into Fish, Microchips and Snowmen, completing just one more train puzzle...or maybe two :)

Flazm Interactive team wishes you happy holidays. See you in 2023!

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/b414e2c5b65df5754614b863474dfdc8e24600d9.png[/img]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2895351287 

Having seven feet of snow cover your neighbourhood in just two days adds a whole new level of difficulty to even most basic delivery jobs-and we don't do basic :) Work your way through the snow dunes, deliver 200 trains, earn at least 3000000 TV2$, remove debris formed by the snowstorm, invest in additional Christmas Tree factories, save the valley from any kind of shortage or isolation the weather could try and introduce and spend 35:59 and less succeeding in all these tasks.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2895465719 

Avoid wrong deliveries and crashing your trains, do not disturb the gigaraffe sanctuary inside the newly developing industrial zone. Ramp up resource extraction, streamline Electricity production and invest in a Van factory; gain access to the second and third levels of the valley, upgrade your engines promptly, follow the 22:30 timer closely-and have fun :) 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2896648457 

No engine upgrades available, timer dangerously close to 16:00 mark and wrong deliveries are waiting to happen left and right-Log Trail fuses Passenger Flow mini-game with high speed Presents deliveries-some recipes require coloured passenger trains and local Lumber Mill is ready to supply every industry in the valley with Wood and Wood accessories :) A fun challenge with lovely scenery.

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/f95c0db3aa0e8a3cc453a3c67d1db75d1b04aeca.png[/img]
Would you look at the time-Choo-Choo Weekly is already here!
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2882450401 

Let's address the chameleon in the room - brimming with colours that refreshingly different design looks good both on Workshop previews and in game. Then we have 30 Passenger Flow trains to take care of, let 4 trains enter wrong stations and spend 1 333 333 TV2$, two quest locations and a layout that makes junction building and train driving all the more fun. LPT'ed. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2884294479

A cyclone of trains is closing in on your location. Do you dare to earn enough, on time and tame the elemental force comprised of several billion Workers trains? DNDATT, 3 bridges to invest in, 10:00. Unconventional, fun little level.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2885439949 

So much to do and-arguably-not enough time (mere 17:00) to spend at least 1 500 000 TV2$, prevent wrong deliveries, complete that multitasking exercise with three quest locations, 12 industries, several supply chains, complete lack of understanding what is a priority at any given moment of time, fastest locomotives ever and an expertly decorated landscape that is worth pushing Pause for a little bit.  

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2884403803 

A classic, familiar to an extent yet obviously brand new DNRT and 220 tiles limit train valley rich with Diamonds, Potatoes and Christmas Trees. A very busy community with 18 delivery quests has an additional quest to successfully connect the city to the railway network while working out a solution to battle the chokepoint in the northwest, beautiful tulip fields to build around coupled with industry locations and recipes that promote gradual expansion and track management and a mammoth family that will take the rest of those 16 minutes you've spent watching flying cars.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/0579c9125e834b12716f07842408022e2f381daf.png[/img]

We are to produce and deliver racing buggies for Island City Motor Racing Circuit championship-we have 19:00 on the timer, directives to avoid train crashes and wrong deliveries from our employers, a starting budget worth a bridge and a half and no plan at all. Yet.

Welcome to Island Racing Track:

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2882937746

MsSalea's train valley presents an advanced vanilla 2018 experience - terrain colouring, industry placement and junction building both encouraged and controlled through decorations and topography design, a supply chain that relies on several resources and goods constantly produced yet offers two Market stations that can be seen as a meaningful way to earn more earlier in the game, useful and affordable train upgrades and shortcuts that look viable - an LPT and several personal playthroughs later all we can say is...

...Well done @MsSalea-they take away both a Level Of The Week and a Level Of The Month, congrachoolations!  Please stand by for a message from our award distribution department.

notes.title: Weekly Winner - October 31st
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/b617657d89e9905a39c535597025d2e29a85f101.png[/img]
Another week - another round of Workshop levels to take a look at.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2880937589 

Santa's Freight Company Inc. has contracted you to maintain delivery schedules in a well-hidden industrial complex somewhere at the North Pole. We'll be using Hyperloops, cold resistant locomotives and virtually unlimited amounts of TV2$ - at least 3 000 000. Of course we have just around 0 TV2$ at the beginning, but nothing some fishing cannot fix :) 41:00, build 2 tunnels, succeed.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2881974899 

A fun Halloween train valley with many routes to plan for and shortcuts to implement as the game progresses and you receive more income, recipes that will send your trains running in circles before that happens, 12:00 timer and no crashes and/or wrong deliveries.  

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2881538934 

A fine scenario with previously undiscovered recipes, top of the line engines, expensive industries and at least 6 bridge sites waiting for our building crews, a landscape that has no place for convenient shortcuts or accidentally spending 75 000 TV2$ on a tunnel because you were too deep in thought and pressed the wrong button :) 14:00, no train crashing allowed.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2879828317 

To make a train valley inside which violet grass will be credible is not enough, but producing a two-level train puzzle with Toll Stations, bodies of orange water obstructing your track building, adding DNRT and DNDATT objectives and combining it all in a specific manner indeed requires labour and thought, a special skill. 13:00, a train puzzle done right.   

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2879931364 

A collaboration with @Blathers and a 16:00 multifacet puzzle that encourages gradual expansion, carefully spending your TV2$ and making sure every train drives to the right station and does not crash on the way there.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2880362660 

Don't go touching anything in the neatly kept garden, keep your track tile count below 170 and find the passage from zone 7 to area 2 ASAP. 14:00, almost unlimited Chocolate and relatively tricky junctions. Happy Birthday!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2882393225

With easy railroad planning out of the picture and no train crashes or wrong deliveries allowed we'll have to keep in mind that not every shortcut is financially viable, depending on your previous decisions and the way you're dealing with Furniture autotrains. A colourful train valley and a great track laying puzzle. I personally failed it twice :)

notes.title: Weekly Winner - October 24th
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/910c1acb749952bb739b99c6056a576b0d2a3056.png[/img]
It's time to assess some Workshop entries.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2877662745 

At 23:00 minutes, with delivery quests increasing quantity demands, lack of spare engines and bridge shortcuts that are going to put a dent in your wallet you could try completing [b]De plateaux en plateaux[/b] only using bridges to connect neighbouring plateaus-no laying tracks down the canyons! DNDATT and DNSAT icons in the top right corner shouldn't discourage you in any way :)

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2878444587 

Generous timers, no train crashes + DNSAT, LPT'ed-[b]Konservy[/b] represents a subgenre of Workshop train valleys that has a special place in your levels-to-return-to queue I'm sure-compact, easy to navigate terrain that immediately suggests possible delivery routes combined with vanilla 2018 early Workshop days aesthetics and hassle-free gratifying gameplay with one delivery location and just 4 quests. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2876924464 and https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2876925013

I've received reports that one could start with the Easy version-figuring that one out makes Hard...well, less hard :) Otherwise just [spoiler]send the first Rocket into the city on Mars and things will pick up the pace from there. [/spoiler] Deliver at least 100 trains, earn 5 000 000 TV2$ or more, watch the 35:00 timer and get your bearings around prebuilt tracks before the Martians get to your candy supply.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2878918453 

Still kind of tricky even with increased 3-stars timer, Halloween Helpers will keep your mouse on the edge of its pad :) DNDATT, hiring both Spiders and Bats to keep the alchemical potioncrafting industrial complex running, interconnecting existing rails in the West and earning enough to pay the Engineers-all the while not buying more than 2 engines. Phew, that one is a very good train puzzle exercise.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2876399370 

20:00, 145 tile limit, demolition jobs budget of 3 100 TV2$-one of the faster, less forgiving valleys that base its gameplay on funds management, gradually growing railway network that connects a new commodity or resource every step of the way, planning ahead of many kinds and distracting the player with picturesque locations.

notes.notes:
Train Valley 2 community is a gem! You are full of creativity and outstanding ideas that help us move forward with the game.

Our railway network is growing fast, and we are close to reaching 2000 community-made levels. We have picked some of the most played weekly and monthly featured levels, balanced and polished them, and created a series of packs called "Train Valley 2 GEMs". We are happy to present the second pack in the series – Train Valley 2: Emerald.

* Experience 50 new levels fully rebuilt and rebalanced
* Enjoy the smart combination of different mechanics and train ages
* Tons of tasks and brain-teasing missions

notes.title: Coming very soon: Emerald and Sapphire level packs, mobile editions
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

A new content update we’d like to present today is a continuation of our GEMS series and includes two separate installments: Emerald Pack and Sapphire Pack.

Both packs contain a number of levels featured by us that were played the most by you, masterfully rebalanced and carefully polished by our in-house designers to bring out the ingenuity and craftsmanship-with every creator’s nickname included into the respective description.

The Emerald DLC with 50 levels inside is out tomorrow, November 16th 2022 at 9 a.m. PST. Wishlist now and enjoy the launch day discount!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2098232/Train_Valley_2_Workshop_Gems__Emerald/

The Sapphire DLC boasting 57 levels is planned for December 7th 2022 - at 9 a.m. PST as well. Feel free to wishlist that one too-we hope the Sapphire pack will last you well past Christmas holidays :)

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2098231/Train_Valley_2_Workshop_Gems__Sapphire/

On to more Train Valley 2 news - you can now enjoy a train puzzle break on the go, anywhere - with our iOS and Android releases! 

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gamegarden.trv2&hl=en&gl=US

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/train-valley-ii/id1621285774

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/3e965f46ed741239e0b06cfd770eee20de0f981e.png[/img]
Several outposts with low quantity but wide resource variety quests, new technologies to put into use with industries available for construction, at least 2 bridges to build and holding down Shift key while deleting tracks-going over the demolition jobs budget of 1 TV2$ is not an option.

It is time to expand your empire in

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2856112380

Upgraded engines and no terraforming-Civilization IV is about steady expansion of your railway system, connecting new industries and combining resources from all over the valley. Congratulations @BenGotham, your €30 Steam gift card is on its way!

notes.title: Weekly Winner - October 17th
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/6c8065c8b173df4444c65a4c2d00a33fb8837586.png[/img]
The Halloween is (almost) upon us, stocking up on candy and finishing your costume are top priorities-but it's as valid a tactic as always to save your strength and work through some train puzzles, don't you think? :)

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2874756632 

The winter is most certainly on its way and multitasking while your final Halloween preparations are underway is a solid plan. Gather your supplies, stockpile local communities, learn how to get Coal and Iron Ore by processing Fish. 30:00, DNSAT, amusez-vous :)

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2875822118 

An oldschool no terraforming medium industry and decorations density tale of fulfilling one's Halloween wishes coupled with heavy duty high volume treats deliveries. Earn at least 2 000 000 TV2$ with a 41:00 timer and destroy 1 TV2$ worth of anything really. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2874059214 

A spinoff of the DooM series, this train valley is full of investment opportunities and magical hazards, tunnel building projects (at least 4!) and generous timers (42:00 for 5 stars to be precise), medium level objects and destinations density and elevated chances of staying up long past your bedtime :)

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2873880324 

DNDATT, 10:00, two autotrains and a whole lot of planning and swift execution holds Feeding Frenzy true to its name-a clever puzzle that tests more than just your choo-chooing skills :)

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2876155659 

No unlimited free Workers this time, we have 1 Market that distributes exactly 4 cars for 2 500 TV2$-Investing In People cultivates careful fund allocation, railway network planning on a per tile basis and train scheduling of the highest precision. 9:00, DNDATT, DNRT, LPT'ed.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2875189039 

A mysterious mud pit that contains Oil, Coal, Iron Ore, Fish, Chocolate and Uranium-truly, every industrialist's dream :) A lot of track building, many trains, and a bit of dynamite is all we need to see this train valley prosper. DNRT, 20:00.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2875643657 

Another train valley set in @Eijolend's Arachnidverse :) Alchemist spider tribe helping our crashlanded explorers tame ancient autofactories-with potioncraft! Do not buy more than 3 engines, 14:00, a chance to start local Paper industry and invest in a Power Plant as a way of saying thank you.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2876088539 

A fine design and a tricky puzzle based on a scene from a very popular space saga. With a 10:00 timer, your task is to deliver explosive payloads and disable the station evading many obstacles-DNDATT, autotrains, local terrain and broken targeting computer :)

Great job @Miaxlo, your €10 Steam gift card is on its way! Please stand by for a message from our award distribution department.
