Hello everyone! The past week has not brought too many new levels, but Choo-Choo Weekly still has to tell you something. Yes, there is only one level here! However, this debut work by @Jasan Quinn definitely deserves your attention.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2237755885
There is a port city and a small town in an isolated valley nearby. The challenge is simple: produce a lot of grain, cattle and canned food to feed both settlements! The playing time is about 15-25 minutes, you will have to build a tunnel and a bridge (or you can do without a bridge). Find the optimal order for sending resources and get all the stars. Great debut, @Jasan Quinn! We are happy to give you a €10 Steam gift card. Congratulations!

As usual, we are waiting for you at our Let's play together challenges. Friends, the start of our October special contest may be delayed for reasons beyond our control. We will definitely keep you informed and will not let you miss this big event. Stay tuned!

notes.title: Weekly Winner - September 21
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/7bb7f8bdd7ced0b9b6ddc4797e86e158108db993.png[/img]
Hello, friends! Choo-Choo Weekly has arrived. There is just over a week left before the October Special Level Design Contest starts, and we have already prepared everything for it! We can't wait to see your levels with all the new features of the future update... But no spoilers! Let's see what our workshop is rich with after last week.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2230781709
@Lasse's debut level. Simple terrain, not too many decorations and obstacles... However, despite its obvious simplicity, this level is pleasant to play. If you are not a fan of challenging levels like [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2231587784]this[/url] and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2233655559]this one[/url], you will definitely like it. Featured!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2233893074
Our regular community member @Zdenek has updated his old level. This map was made more than two years ago and many probably don't remember it anymore. So it can be considered new! @Zdenek expects that one day this map will be used for our traditional Let's play together challenges and who knows, maybe this will happen one day…

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2230945051
Today's winner is a level from our other longtime author. @unclekrusty started making maps when we first launched our workshop. And we are glad to see his new works today! This level touched our hearts: it is dedicated to the 5th anniversary of the release of the first Train Valley. This game has found a place in the hearts of many people, it has many fans. For some, it marks a special period in life, and some people, thanks to it and a couple of random events, found a new profession (like the author of these lines, haha). Sentiments aside, this level has good gameplay. And have you seen this gorgeous cake? It is impossible to resist! @unclekrusty, thanks for your work, we are incredibly moved and happy to give you a €10 Steam gift card.

That’s all for today. We are going to prepare announcements and write the rules of the new contest. Follow the news!

notes.title: Weekly Winner - September 14
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/30d2dad2bff201ef70d2a5172efd917a0becdc60.png[/img]
Hello! September has already approached its equator. In the meantime, our authors seem to be gathering strength for the October special level design contest. Anyway, we think so because last week there were only 2 levels in the workshop. However, it was difficult for us to choose the best one!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2227216725
Winter is coming to the forest kingdom and we need to prepare supplies. This is unusual, but mainly gold and its products will warm people this winter. Well, there must be some magic involved! Otherwise, why do they need these devices, glass, and sand?.. Thanks for this interesting map with many bridges, @LittleBear!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2222560277
Today's favorite is an unusual level by @Itsumi-chan, which you will surely play more than once. Briefing: no pause, no train stops, 3 slow locomotives. In such conditions, you have to find the best routes and intelligently distribute the delivery of all resources. You have 15 minutes, but this map will surely take you at least half the evening. Whatever it is, it's worth it! Great puzzle, @Itsumi-chan, we are pleased to give you a €10 Steam gift card.

That's all! As usual, we are waiting for you in our traditional Let's play together competitions. Stay tuned!

notes.title: Weekly Winner - September 07
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/9317a184b2cec964ac1c75a867c04aa7b54b0084.png[/img]
Hello friends! One more week is behind us and we are ready to tell you about the best works of the beginning of September. Our selection today has levels for every taste: short and long, simple and difficult. Let's see!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2219148794
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2222314589
Did @gayetemp's mom know she would make a big contribution to our level collection? Unlikely, however, we see more and more new stories about her and about the old cities of the United Kingdom. @gayetemp made a new map and told another great story about her homeland. This is not the easiest level: in one version, you cannot use pause, in another, you cannot stop trains. We couldn't decide which is better, so you'll find both of these in the Featured.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2220551456
A small puzzle by @LittleBear. You have pieces of this puzzle ‒ sand islands, and you need to connect them so that all colored passenger trains can reach any station. No wrong deliveries! A beautiful and warm level for these cool autumn days.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2217710448
Maestro @The Good, The Bad and The Dudley is here again! We missed you. And we're sure you, too, have missed his long levels, which are so appropriate for dark evenings. (Okay, this noir is more for the northern hemisphere.) This is the classic one-hour level of Mr. Dudley: you have multiple functional areas, you start with the production of primary resources and gradually move further and further. Don't be intimidated by the toll stations ‒ you can definitely afford it.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2219897841
And here is the best level of the week. @thomas recalls Mr. Dudley's long-standing trick: you have no start-up capital, you have to sell some property to build the first stretch of tracks. Here it is implemented gracefully, you do not have to look for random items, just start building tracks and you will have money. Apart from that, this level has excellent gameplay. There is a choice, there are limitations, there is a strict timing that forces you to look for optimal ways. Great job, @thomas! A €10 Steam gift card is deservedly yours.

It's been a great week! We have already started preparing the October special contest. Until then, we keep the same schedule: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/3148519255758118685/]extra Let’s play together challenge[/url] on Tuesday and main [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/1640912759106326420/]Let’s play together challenge[/url] on Friday. See you, friends!

notes.title: Level of the Month - August 2020
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/b8ca7620a6e825989396412ba94623a612bd5f22.png[/img]
Hello everyone! Another month passed and we again chose the best level. In July, we held a special contest under the Minimalism motto: we demanded the authors to make simple levels no more than 10 minutes long. We expected people to miss the long levels after that and the levels would last an average of 30 minutes throughout August :) However, in the workshop we continue to find short levels with excellent gameplay and laconic decoration. Did you like them too? Today we will present to you the winner of August and this is exactly that level.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2194199930
Dried contaminated land, industrial enterprises are chaotically spread over it. But once you start laying out tracks, you will discover how many moves you can make on this map. There are a lot of challenges for the player here: you cannot upgrade trains and you have to decide how to allocate the unusual amount of resources. This is a very laconic and at the same time deeply thought-out work. Congratulations @embRellish! We are happy to give you a €30 Steam gift card.

We are already planning a special design contest in October. Maybe you have ideas about it? We'd love to see your suggestions in the comments!

notes.title: Weekly Winner - August 31
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/33f00c0547513b277f370b93a1ea82c5f4e68ab9.png[/img]
Hello! Choo-Choo Weekly has arrived again. It seems that summer has started quite recently, but today it ends. Therefore, we are in a hurry to tell you about the best works in our workshop over the past week, so that you can enjoy your first autumn evenings this year.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2209430330
A slightly insane level by @Itsumi-chan that you are unlikely to complete on the first try. Also, we do not guarantee you that your second attempt will be successful too. It will also be quite difficult for you to figure out how to complete this level if you do not read the description. Well, we'll help you a little: see that park block, which requires 999 units of dynamite? Before the last train with resources enters the depot, remove this park. Done, you are a winner. You will find this unusual and challenging level in the Featured to come back to it again and again.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2209069157
@gayetemp invites you on a journey through Wales in the mid-20th century (presumably). On the way, you will see everything: beautiful nature, many animals, castles and narrow roads without the possibility of turning. You will have to understand the complex system of tracks and in no way damage anything: the beauty of Wales must remain intact. Brew a large teapot, as this is a very large and deeply detailed map that will take you all evening. Thanks for the tour, @gayetemp!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2208621164
Small map with roundabout traffic. This is where you have to puzzle over how to connect the sand quarry to the main road, but this problem has a solution. Well balanced level lasting 14 minutes. Great job, @embRellish! A €10 Steam gift card is yours.

Very soon we will choose the best level of August, but first we need to prepare another [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/3148519255758118685/]extra Let’s play together challenge[/url] for you. Stay tuned, friends!

notes.title: Weekly Winner - August 24
notes.notes:

Hello! Another good week is behind us and again we are in a hurry to tell you about the most interesting levels from our workshop. We have new authors, and we are very happy about that. Let's see what debutants and experienced level designers prepared for us!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2206115395
Is this a Train Valley map? This is a map of the world! Small level with continents and trains, and the main resource is plastic. You only have 5 minutes, hurry up. Great job, @sabrinalynn23! Featured.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2203299591
Do you miss the old games? Where the player has to hone their skills for a long time and diligently so as not to fail in the first 30 seconds. Meet the Retro Game by @gayetemp! https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2207020315

notes.title: Weekly Winner - August 18
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/68b6529274fdc743c769148808b1aad58708eb8d.png[/img]
Hello friends! Another issue of Choo-Choo Weekly is here. Many interesting levels continue to appear in our workshop and we, as always, are glad to tell you about the brightest ones. Completing the levels from our today selection will take you a lot of time, so free up your evening. Let’s see!

A gloomy place among ruins, a cemetery, and a dump of rusty trains. You have slow trains, you need wood and sand. A simple good map in case you don't have too much free time. Featured!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2186057757

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2192463420
Nice level with interesting gameplay. Three cities, few resources, different routes. notes.title: Level of the Month - July 2020 and special contest winners
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/e108d202db92d679d29c019b1f666aa3589d7143.png[/img]
Hello friends! July special design contest has ended and it’s time to name the winners. We want to remind you of the main conditions of this contest: levels should be short (up to 10 minutes) and they should be minimalistic. This is a broad definition and everyone can understand it differently. We expected to see levels with minimalistic art designs, or levels with simple gameplay, or a small variety of resources. Or all of these things at the same time. Anyway, over the past month, we have discovered many forms of minimalism from our authors and we are happy to see so many beautiful works in the workshop. Now we have to do the hardest thing - choose the best maps!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2178618332
Small map with many power plants. The focus of the game is shifted from resource extraction to energy extraction (which also requires resources, however). Nice simple art design and unusual gameplay. @Phil.方阵, we're happy to give you a €10 Steam gift card for your debut work! Congratulations!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2167199149
Colorblock-styled map by our LPT Champion @stev1eb. Excellent gameplay, interesting boost at the beginning of the game. There are opportunities to optimize the speed of walkthrough of the level. It looks like @stev1eb hasn't received any prizes in a while - hopefully a €20 Steam gift card will fix that.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2181619645
The undisputed winner of the past month. This level has it all: simple and elegant art, storyline, few resources, and many ways to optimize. In addition, this map has excellent timing. This level is like a well-cooked dish with the perfect balance of salt, sugar and acid. Congratulations, @YaroslavTV, today you are the chef! A €30 Steam gift card is yours!

It was a great month and a great contest! We are sure that such unusual conditions made authors look at the creation of levels differently. Our traditional design contest continues, we are waiting for your new levels, friends. See you!

notes.title: Weekly Winner - August 03
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/22b6179f15fc0571c0ade74876f66dfef389b398.png[/img]
Hello everyone! Our special July Level Design Contest ended last week. In recent days, a lot of impressive works have been uploaded to our workshop. The latest issue of Train Valley Time will be released very soon, and now it is the time to sum up the last week. Let's go!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2180807293
The second work of last week's debutant @embRellish. Interesting map with variable routes. Be careful, trains with the bears are very fast!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2179406469
New level by @Gelledee with many bridges and tunnels. Don't waste money on trains - new colored stations are constantly appearing here and they will require bridges.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2180797889
Hot sandy map by Maestro @h2onik. Fast train updates, lots of gold and oil, and a good balance of toll and one-way stations. Great level!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2182821168
Large-scale work by Maestro @striker700. The author invites the player to figure out priorities and this really makes the map very versatile. You have several zones and directions, you can act on your own, and in any way you choose you will come to success. Very beautiful map. It's pleasant to dive into its gameplay and to study it over and over again. You will find it in the Featured.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2181568294
@embRellish keeps making levels and every new one gets better! Another short level: there are colored stations and factories. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2179778263
Another level by @striker700. As usual, it is very beautiful - even if @striker700's levels are too difficult for you, you can just enjoy their looks. You need to build a bridge in time for the trains to go to the upper steel factory, and then to the cliff. So dramatic!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2181619645
And this is the best level of the week! It has a very good balance and design. Minimalistic art, not too many resources, good timing. You can play this level using different routes and look for the most optimal one. Great job, @YaroslavTV! A €10 Steam gift card is yours!

notes.title: Weekly Winner - July 27

notes.title: July special level design contest
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/68d57f11193457ba16d2045abe4b63c3f4bbcba8.png[/img]
Hello friends! We are happy to announce the start of the July Special Level Design Contest. In the past months, for such special contests, we added some new objects to the level editor. Now we are busy developing another new game, so there will be no new object. But we decided to set up special conditions for the contest levels.

The main idea of this contest is minimalism. We want to see simple short levels. We plan to use them in the future Let's Play Together challenges, so we set a limit on the duration of the level: no more than 10 minutes to get all stars. In addition, we want the authors not to think about our fast champions and take care of slower players. Please set the timings so that many players can get 5 stars. We are sure that this rigid framework will open up great freedom for creativity.
 
As usual, we will reward the top three levels. Winners will receive Steam gift cards with a face value of €30, €20 and €10 for 1, 2 and 3 places respectively. We wish you good luck and inspiration!

notes.title: The 1000th level
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/0bc9d9964cc61d66b02ffc44d37d102f96affdc6.png[/img]
Hello friends! We have wonderful news: the 1000th level has been uploaded to our workshop! We were looking forward to this event. At the same time, we were not ceasing to be amazed at how many players make levels. We have a thousand amazing levels! We want to tell you a little about the most outstanding authors and for this, we came up with several nominations.

[h3]Most Productive Author[/h3]
@The Good, The Bad and The Dudley made 140 levels for our workshop and it was he who made the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2126070051/]1000th level[/url]. He has been making levels since the workshop was introduced and it seems he is not going to stop.

[h3]Most Award-Winning Author[/h3]
This step of the podium is shared by @The Good, The Bad and The Dudley and @striker700. Each of them has 12 awards. By the way, @striker700’s level became [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1694810664/]the level of 2019[/url].

[h3]Most Popular Level[/h3]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1416586135/]Abandoned Oil Rig[/url] was made 2 years ago and to this day remains the most popular level. 7484 people subscribed to it, 1800 people gave a positive rating to this map.

[h3]Lead Guide Author[/h3]
@h2onik is an unusual author. She is the second most productive author of our workshop after @The Good, The Bad and The Dudley, with a whopping [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198050371490/myworkshopfiles/?appid=602320&sort=score&browsefilter=myfiles&view=imagewall/]58 levels[/url]. However, many of her levels are unusual in that in addition to interesting gameplay and art design, they tell us about some places, phenomena, or interesting people. In her workshop, you will find levels about the Glacier Express, about the Polish engineer Ernest Malinowski, as well as stories about the Olympic gods. We also used @h2onik’s levels for Let's Play Together challenges more often than any other author’s levels: 7 times.

[h3]Most Efficient Author[/h3]
Of the 18 levels made by @striker700, 8 were awarded. Good ratio!

[h3]The Craziest Level[/h3]
You may doubt our choice, but we believe that [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2016337499/]this level by @PureSativa[/url] is the craziest in our workshop. Just look: there are 59 stores, from which trains leave at different intervals. You have to figure out (or guess) in what order these stores should be launched in order to complete the level in 40 minutes. In any case, the level will end precisely at this time. We tried to finish it for 5 stars, but after a few attempts we gave up. If you know more insane levels in our workshop, write about them in the comments to this post!

Hello friends! Another month has come to an end and we are pleased to sum it up. In May, there were many good levels from our regular authors, from new ones, and from those who returned to this craft after a break. The applicants were stronger than ever, but we have to choose only one and it is...

...Resource Islands! A level with amazing gameplay. It captures you for 13 minutes and uses all your mental resources. Yes, it is these resources that the islands really need. We also want to note the concise and high-quality art design. @BlaiddL3g3nd, we have played your level many times (not only because of hard timing) and we are absolutely sure that you deserve a €30 Steam gift card. Congratulations!

Our contest continues! We hope that in June the number of excellent maps in the workshop will reach 1000. We will be very happy about this event! In the meantime, we are waiting for you at our fun Let's Play Together challenges. More and more people are playing together, recently the number of participants has exceeded 100 people. Only you are missing! Stay tuned, friends.

notes.title: Update #31 - Gamepad Support
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/277c5b17b8a3412493778209ae11742b314236a9.png[/img]
Hello friends! I hope you are well! We have great news. We used to think that train games are keyboard and mouse only. So if you like train management games please play them at the table and even thing about couch gaming. We are here to break this stereotype and introduce you to full gamepad support for Train Valley 2. Maybe it will seem a bit strange at the beginning, but probably after 5 minutes, it will be your favorite way to play the game! What I can say for sure: it is much easier to build tracks with a gamepad! Try it out! There is no special gamepad tutorial yet, but you should easily get the idea of the control scheme from the hints.

[h3]What is added?[/h3]
- Full Gamepad support (Xbox 360, Xbox One, PS4, PS3, and [url=https://guavaman.com/projects/rewired/docs/SupportedControllers.html]many many others[/url])
- Timings and challenges added to workshop levels description.

[h3]What is fixed?[/h3]
- Wrong hint for Embargo station.
-  Scroll added for workshop level description in the game browser. The font size stays the same. 
- Unity engine updated to the last version (more optimized and stable).

Please share the feedback about your gamepad user experience and in case you face any bugs or problems. We are here to help as always!
Stay tuned and be safe! ːtvmachinistː

UPD: If you experience problems with the keyboard or mouse controls you can always choose "previous_stable" build in BETA section (right-click on the game in Steam library > Properties > BETA).

notes.title: Update #29 - Embargo Station
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/41ceeb0245e9bb902c40cee2b17a9163b4adc719.png[/img] Hello friends! Hope you and your family are safe. We have prepared something really interesting for you with this update. Ladies and gentlemen, please meet [b]Embargo Station[/b]. This new level editor object has very simple mechanics. It allows all the goods to come through except one (you can set it in level editor settings). This is a flexible and powerful mechanics offering a lot of interesting situations. We want to thank @Yokuyin from our community for offering this great idea! And we are looking forward to seeing what you guys can create with the new Embargo Station!

[h3]APRIL LEVEL DESIGN CONTEST - EMBARGO STATION[/h3]
We are adding extra prizes and a theme of our level design contest in April. Create a workshop level with Embargo Station during the April and win a 30€, 20€ or 10€ Steam card! No jokes!
 
We have also finished some long-awaited in-game browser functionality making easier to find the best workshop levels among >800 of them. Full list of changes:

[h3]What is new?[/h3]
- Embargo Station object in Level Editor.
- Sorting by Author option in workshop in-game browser.
- "Recently Played First" sorting option (will work only after this update, but definitely help you later)
- Autosave in the level editor (will carefully save your work every minute).
- Discord button near the active let's-play-together level in the main menu. Now it's easier to participate in the contest and join our warm discord community).

[h3]What is fixed?[/h3] 
- A bug allowed tracks to be built across the one-way station object.
- A bug with missing tracks on the one-way station entrance.
- Interface scale problem in the main menu.

Please let us know if something goes wrong with this update. We are here to help!
Don't forget to create great levels (just try if you never did) and participate in our let-play-together events. Now we have two of them every week!

notes.title: Level of the Month - February 2020 and special contest winners
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/78a1344b2721c2a52318f97f3e98d1a712e66e51.png[/img]
Hello friends! The February special level design contest is over. We examined many good levels, we saw many new authors, and it makes us happy. As always, it was difficult to choose because many maps deserve to win. But we are really happy with our decision. So, here is our verdict!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2006633161
The debut of @brainstorm4. The trains are in the role of city taxis. They scurry along the narrow streets of the metropolis, many of these roads are one-way. Great job, @brainstorm4! We are happy to give you a €10 Steam gift card. And we are waiting for new levels!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1999397378
@Rock98 is also the discovery of recent weeks. At first, there were very simple levels, then they were more complex and interesting. And now "the green land" has become one of the best levels of the month! It is very interesting to play this level. Different mechanics are very harmoniously mixed here; the landscape is also well designed. @Rock98, €20 Steam gift card is deservedly yours!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2003156133
@Gelledee is the absolute winner of the February special contest. In addition to the combination of all the latest mechanics and excellent visuals, this level best demonstrates the features and capabilities of a one-way station. Great gameplay. @Gelledee, you did an amazing job! We congratulate you on your victory and give a €30 Steam gift card.

Uh, that was a hot month! In March, we will continue our regular level design contest as usual. We need some rest, and then we will definitely come up with an occasion for a new special contest! Follow the news, go to [url=https://discord.gg/train-valley]our Discord server[/url] and be sure to take part in our weekly [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/1640912759106326420/]Let’s play together[/url].

notes.title: Level of the Month - January 2020
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/5071487984fd1d9a3c868aa8a019845d91a981f8.png[/img]
Hello everyone! While our authors are studying the new one-way station mechanic and coming up with new levels with it, we are going to sum up the results of January. We unanimously decided that the main prize of the month will go to our new author: meet @Gelledee!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1965493941
@Gelledee laid down many route options. In this level, you will build a lot of bridges and over time you can rebuild them, creating new routes. This is reminiscent of the stairs in Hogwarts: they are constantly changing directions and almost intersect with themselves. Great gameplay, of course. @Gelledee has other good levels. We are waiting for your new work, and now we are happy to give you the €30 Steam gift card! Congratulations!

Friends, each of you can get on the cover of Train Valley Time. Just open the level editor and try to make a small nice map. You will surely enjoy it! And we will go to play new contest levels. See you later!

notes.title: Update 28 - One Way Station
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/3c17fc16be085249da1360546e9beec98872dcf4.png[/img]
Hello friends! I hope you are doing good this crazy year! If you get tired from all those news about WW3 and coronavirus and want to take a little break we have a great opportunity. Try to play with our new workshop object called "One Way Station". You can find it in Level Editor in "Stations" folder. It is a simple yet powerful element, that allows trains to go only one direction. We believe that this object can help to build a lot of interesting situations and can dramatically change the rules of gameplay. So let it be a theme of February level design contest. Build a level with "One way station" and upload it to the Workshop till the end of February. 3 best levels will get a prizes from our team!


[h3]What is new?[/h3]
- New workshop object: "One way station".

[h3]What is fixed?[/h3]
- Bug allowing to build a new bridge on the top of the drawbridge.
- Objects "DesertCity4" and "DesertCity5" are not deletable any more.
- Bug with "Space Age" achievement.
- Problem with launching downloaded workshop maps in offline mode.

Please let us know if you face any problems. We are here to help as always!
Stay tuned! Choo-Choo!

notes.title: Summary 2019
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/ce75680c9b8d2b0a8e714ffef28e724ae866235c.png[/img]

Hello dear friends! Our sweet Train Valley family! This amazing year was full of pleasant events and occasions! 
First of all, we have finally released the full version of the game in April. Do you remember your first TV2 rocket launched? Amazing moment!
After this year, we had a great summer marathon developing and releasing Passenger Flow DLC in October! 20 more levels, new (or good old) mechanics and a lot of stuff for Workshop! What a time!

But the real gold is our lovely, creative community! Just imagine right now we have 729 levels in the Workshop. 209 of them are featured! 64 of them are using new passenger flow mechanics! You are doing an amazing job, friends! All of you: @alphrost, @h2onik, @striker700, @reg, @Gaztibelza, @unclekrusty, @Nimu, @sarahfmorgan, @gemanera, and many many others! We are proud to have you among our honored authors! 
But there is one creator reached a 100 maps record! We are talking about you, @Mr Dudley. I don't know how you find time for that, but you are our hero!
We are truly proud of Train Valley 2 Workshop and it's only because of your amazing work guys!

To support your creativity we sent 93 Stem gift cards and keep doing it every week and month. We keep making weekly newspapers "Choo-choo weekly" and monthly covers "Train Valley Time" in your honor! I hope you are [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/602320/discussions/1/1640912759106355285/]reading them[/url]!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/3801d16d5914d0f940a56f9124e55e8529353ced.jpg[/img]
This year we have started and keep arranging let's play together contests. We did it 45 weeks in a row already. And we have an amazing champion here as well. It is @stev1eb who collected the first 18 cards of the original set and now all 26 cards of the expanded set of cards. He was a champion in 12 of Let's play together contests! And get an exclusive knitted locomotive from our team! Congratulations!
But there are a lot of other cool guys and girls gathering every Friday on our [url=https://discord.gg/train-valley]Discord server[/url]: @Yokuyin (your [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1658352270]guide[/url] is amazing), @Gamma Is Evil, @Unicast, @Nomiswelt, @Zebrakatten, @LiveConnector and many others! Thanks for keeping contests that friendly warm and challenging!
  
And of cause great thanks to our team. Thanks to Olga aka @glyinderwust for her hard and dedicated work as a community manager and her superior Workshop maps! Have you read her [url=https://us8.campaign-archive.com/?u=6ae3c9563c24bc8261157ef70&id=5d26ed4284]newsletter[/url]? It's worth your time! Our level designer Anton, 3d modeler Timofey and programmer Sergey did an amazing job! Special thanks to Alexander Ahura for the new DLC soundtrack! It's an honor to work with you guys! 

Happy new year to everyone in the Train Valley family! Warmest wishes to you and yours! 
It is just the beginning! Stay tuned! Choo Choo!
- Alxey Davydov aka Flazm

notes.title: Results of Passenger Flow Level Design Contest
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28520888/9f90bf57c57a58d5d7f7d91ee044aaec871db74b.png[/img]
Hello everyone! We are finally ready to announce the results of the contest. We got about 30 levels and only after a long discussion we were able to choose 3 of them.

So, the third place and €10 Steam gift card go to @h2onik.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1895328151
This is a very dynamic level that requires maximum concentration from the player. It is an unusual and pretty map. We liked the clever use of hyperloops. We also like the fresh idea and the short duration of this level.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1891233351
We got a lot of good levels from our longtime author @The Good, The Bad and The Dudley. And it is this level that best demonstrates the principle of a constant shortage of resources invented by him. For this, Dudley very accurately calculated and tuned the order of the appearance of new colored stations ‒ they are always ahead of your possibilities and put you before the choice: to buy a bridge or a train? Great job, maestro, €20 Steam gift card is yours!

The best gameplay was shown by @Yokuyin.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1902730413
But in addition to excellent gameplay, we enjoyed the decoration of this level. The earth seems to be painted with watercolors with its smooth gradients, and factories and colored stations are precisely color-matched to their locations. This level is carefully thought out in every detail and we unanimously awarded the victory to it. Congratulations, @Yokuyin! We are happy to give you a €30 Steam gift card.

In addition, we would like to highlight the level of @striker700 in a special nomination.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1894450228
Great design and unusual use of decorative objects! We enjoyed looking at this map. Thank you for this work, we give you a €10 Steam gift card.

We also liked another work of @h2onik.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1884322848
This is a simple and excellent demonstration of the mechanics of colored trains. We believe that everyone who has not tried colored stations should start from this level.

It was a great contest! We want to say a big thank you to all the authors. You are incredibly talented people! We wish to see your new levels in the workshop. See you later!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1826606347 @SanSanych offers us to go into a deep gorge, rich in gold ore. Grab a pickaxe: you'll have to lay the rails along a lot of winding slopes. You will have to think hard about the schedule of your locomotive fleet: stopping trains is forbidden, and the distances they have to cover are very long. And, of course, do not forget to look for shortcuts. Great job, @SanSanych, the level is deservedly sent to Featured!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1828930350 The debut work of @scott.jackson. You are in a small, cozy valley where a variety of resources regularly arrive on schedule: from workers to computers. You can’t take all of them right away, and be careful, ring trains can sometimes interfere with new ones leaving the tunnels. Let's face it: this is a level for experienced players. But we really liked the thoughtful work with the relief and the decoration. Great start, @scott.jackson, we would like to see more of your levels! And you will find this map in Featured.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1827066379 On top of the podium today is @tehrealyoyo. Here are multi-tiered dunes, among which there is an active mining of ore. You have two cities and many forks and hidden passages that you can use in various combinations. One of the tasks is to build many bridges, but you would not have resisted the temptation anyway. Try to find the best routes among a whole bunch of options, but no train stops! Very thoughtful work and excellent gameplay. We are happy to give @tehrealyoyo a €10 Steam Gift Card.

These are the results of the past week. Do not forget to sort the levels in the workshop according to the date of addition, in addition to the Featured there are many unusual maps. Their number approaches six hundred and many of the most incredible ideas are embodied in these maps. “Gods, how did the author come to this decision?!” is our favorite feeling ;) And we are sure that we will experience it more than once. Hello friends! Your Ferris wheel cabin has slowly come next to Monday, and as always, the fresh issue of Choo-Choo Weekly falls on your knees. Last week, only three maps were added to the workshop, but they are excellent!  With great pleasure, we hurry to tell you about them.

You are preparing to go IPO, however, due to the fact that you have little experience in this matter, your friends advise you to be ready for failure and stock up on instant noodles. Well, you can only hope that they will generously share some boiling water with you :) But we think you have every chance of success. You will definitely like the dizzying landscape, high-speed trains will run like a roller coaster in an amusement park. Good job, @angryxpeh, map’s place is in Featured!

If this is an advertisement, then it is very good! Indeed, the atmosphere is recreated with great accuracy: coal productions of all kinds are everywhere, thermal power plants are in the center of the valley and people are arriving. Well, try to warm everyone here and save Manchester. Elaborate work, @莫高雷蒙牛, definitely Featured!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1773609524 The central place today is occupied by maestro @h2onik with no less elaborate work "Ghost towns". If you do not have the habit of reading the description of the level before its first launch, then you probably will not notice what makes it so special and what the huge hangar is. However, together with Craig Mazin, @h2onik puts another monument to human errors, on which it is important to work and remember them for the sake of the future. Using the standard objects in the level editor, the author has created an exact miniature of an overgrown abandoned city with its Soviet five-story buildings and the famous Ferris wheel. Of course, the huge hangar is New Safe Confinement over the 4th power unit of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, which was finished just 2 years ago. Move back in time a little and help finish it! Of course, it requires a lot of workers and engineers, as well as metal and other building materials. You will have to transport workers from afar because there is still almost no one in the exclusion zone... Thank you for such an important level, @h2onik, your victory today is unconditional. The €10 Steam Gift Card goes to neighboring Poland!

It seems that this is all that we wanted to tell you today. Take care of yourself and your loved ones and look for inspiration in everything that surrounds you. With the help of our level editor you can create your own story and tell us what is important to you. We are always waiting for your work. See you soon, friends!

Green meadows are in front of you as if descended from canvases of pastoral painters that you have to bring to life with threads of railways. Traditional animal husbandry is complemented by the production of printed materials, because each inhabitant of these small towns needs to relax in the evenings with a book in their hands in their lush garden. If you love Italy just like @Giangi7723, then you can find other maps about this beautiful country on the author's Steam page!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1763314839 The author of 50 levels of the main campaign of the game, @Grem made an excellent level for the workshop, or rather, specifically for our competition [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/602320/announcements/detail/1595877398596979476]Let’s play together[/url]. Looking at the name of the map, you can probably guess who will look at you from this quiet picturesque lake. @Grem offers you a choice of a whole bunch of options for completing this level, and during the day that the competition lasted, it seemed to us that the competition with such maps should be extended 2 times so that there is enough time for everyone to try and hone all the routes and find the most optimal one. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1762600208 The new map from @h2onik is like a box under the Christmas tree in December: whatever is hidden in it, it will definitely be a pleasant surprise. And the current box amazed us! In it, we found a fantastic story about a Polish engineer who was invited to Peru to build a railway and designed an amazing route that connected the Pacific and Atlantic oceans through the Andes. This was a real engineering marvel (by the standards of the second half of the 19th century;  however, even now this road is impressive) that included dozens of tunnels, bridges and viaducts, and also ran at an altitude of over 4800 meters above sea level! Construction was carried out in incredibly difficult conditions and @h2onik very accurately reflected this in her work ‒ destruction and rockfalls were a frequent occurrence. We are sure that it would not be an exaggeration to say that this map is another monument to Ernest Malinovsky from his compatriot and a fan of railways. We are extremely happy to learn such fascinating stories through the levels in the workshop and are happy to give @h2onik Steam gift card with a par value of €10. Bravo!

notes.title: Locomotive 6-2 (The Bullet)
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28520888/f17746f8a64465111f0a3e2771b2276d1485937d.png[/img] Good day, train lovers! The day has come: we have arrived at the final station, where the last locomotive is waiting for you, the one that inspired us to create a game model. We have come a long way and at the end of it we get such a bright specimen of the railway progress. If you have played first Train Valley, you probably remember its predecessor, the fastest green handsome Shinkansen E5. Today we will meet its younger relative: Shinkansen E6 Series!

[h1]The Bullet Trains - E6 Series Shinkansen[/h1]
If we’re talking about high-speed trains, there’s only one place where this trip should end to come full circle: the very place where they started speeding up, that is, Japan. The first true high-speed train was the Tokaido Shinkansen, which began service in 1964 just a few days before the Tokyo Olympics. It was a real revolution! For the first time, it was possible to go back and forth Tokyo and Osaka, the two largest Japanese cities, in the same day: it started as a 4 hours trip, but in just a few months they managed to shorten it to three hours and ten minutes. 

This train was quickly nicknamed “the Bullet Train” for the bullet-like shape of its nose. It was an immediate success – so much that it changed the whole way of making business in Japan, and the life of the Japanese as a whole since it allowed day work trips between these two capital cities for their economy. In less than three years it reached the 100 million passenger mark – and an impressive figure of one billion passengers in 1976. Its success convinced the authorities to extend the high-speed rail network – and it was a living example of success that helped to convince the world of the advantages of high-speed rails. Without the shade of a doubt, this is one of the many instances of train transportation well implemented changing society for good. 

[img]https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4a/E611-1.jpg[/img] (Photo from [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E6_Series_Shinkansen#/media/File:E611-1.jpg]Wikipedia[/url])

The E6 series is their latest evolution. The first bullet trains ran at a maximum of 210 km/h; today’s Shinkansen are capable of reaching a max speed of 320 km/h. In order to reach their famed speed and regularity, the Shinkansen employs some of the most advanced technology. For a start, their rail lines are completely separated from conventional lines and designed to help trains reach their full potential with as few curves as possible. It has the usual Bo’Bo’ wheel arrangement of these trains; its engines use (via pantograph) a highly powered overhead in order to overcome the limitations of the direct current that power the Japanese electrified rails. 

We’re talking about engines because, as happens with lots of high-speed trains, the E6 Shinkansen doesn’t have a locomotive as such; instead, each car is individually powered, which allows for faster acceleration and deceleration. This is very important for the Shinkansen since it has more stops than any other high-speed train in the world; it needs that extra kick so as not to lose too much time with every stop. And the living testament of the advanced technology of the Shinkansen is its safety: in his whole history, the Shinkansen trains never have had an accident. The E6 series, the one operating as of today, started its service in March 2013 and has no expiration date yet.

Its in-game counterpart has the same sleek, nimble features that make the Bullet Trains look like something directly from a sci-fi movie… and of course, its iconic bullet-shaped nose. This train is ready to take you all the way to the future without even slowing down – and in the most comfortable ride of your life too! 

In the past months, we’ve come a long way. We started our trip in the early days of train transportations, discovering some of the iconic locomotives of the Steam Golden Era. We saw these monsters of coal and smoke evolving into faster and more efficient machines, then switching to diesel to travel through mountains and plains all across the world. As time passed trains became cleaner with electric-powered locomotives; then high-speed trains came and started spreading all over the world. And afterward? Who knows what the future will bring, but this we know: there will be trains in it! 

It’s been a wonderful journey: we’ve enjoyed a lot writing this historical vignettes, and we hope you had fun discovering the trains that inspired the ones you can use in the game.  Thanks a lot for joining us for this trip and for playing Train Valley 2, of course. May your trains run fast, safe, and on time!

notes.title: Locomotive 6-2 (The Champion)
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28520888/92a747272dcdc64b3ab222d9cd9bb80c0ab3733e.png[/img] Good day, train lovers! This is the last station before our final destination: today and in the next post, we’ll have a look at the historical counterparts of the very last two locomotives you can find in Train Valley 2. We’re looking into present day now: these are trains that you can easily find and ride. Comparatively clean, insanely fast, and safest than ever, today’s trains are small moving marvels of cutting-edge technology. For the first leg of this journey we’re going to France, so brace yourselves, for this train goes really fast!

[h1]The TGV POS[/h1]
The TGV is the whole line of French high-speed trains (the letters stand just for “Train à Grand Vitesse”). Its first prototype was built in 1969 and funny enough they worked with gas turbines (basically burning gas oil to produce energy) instead of electricity. Regardless of their performance, the 1973 energy crisis prompted the French authorities to discard this prototype, deeming it to be uneconomic. On the other hand, France had started building nuclear power stations all over the country, so there was plenty of (comparatively) cheap electricity to be used…

So, in the end, their engineers turned to electricity from overhead lines and took many of the new technologies developed for the failed TGV 001, like high-speed brakes, aerodynamics, and new signaling systems. Several years later, the first electric prototype was completed and deployed for testing, and after some trials, the French administration decided to commit to the TGV project and started to fund it for good. In 1980 the first high-speed line was opened. After a few years, a good part of the French territory was covered by high-speed rails; in 1994, the Eurostar service connected continental Europe to London crossing the Channel Tunnel.

[img]https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a6/SNCF_TGV4409_Liestal_010809.jpg[/img] (Photo from [url=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a6/SNCF_TGV4409_Liestal_010809.jpg]Wikipedia[/url])

The POS itself is in service since 2006; it is a curious specimen, having been built by connecting single-deck carriages of the earlier TGV Réseau with new power cars – and the now free TGV Réseau power cars are also in use with other carriages in hybrid sets, so the Réseau spawned not one but two “lineages” of high-speed trains. The POS power cars have the particularity of being asynchronous: in case of failure, the broken engine can be isolated in order to make the rest work without its output, thus allowing it to reach the station to get fixed without interrupting the service.

The TGV is famed for its safety: it has never suffered a major accident in its entire history. But that’s not the only reason for its fame: it’s also insanely fast. The POS itself is a record-breaking train: in 2007 it set a new world speed record on conventional rails, reaching up to 574.8 km/h. Because the train was slightly modified for these trials, it is considered a somehow unofficial record – but this max speed is still impressive, especially when combined with the safety record of the TGV in general. So if you ever ride a TGV, enjoy the ride without worrying for a second at how fast you’re going!

Our in-game counterpart keeps the same slender, elegant lines, with the bullet-shaped nose and wide frontal window. You can also recognize its long and stretch lateral windows. It’s name is Champion, and you can guess why. This train won’t stop at anything to get you to your destination – and fast!

That's all for today! We have only one stage left to reach the final station, where we will get acquainted with the last high-speed train. It is truly legendary and is absolutely worthy to complete our long journey through the milestones of the history of train development. For us, railways are a very special world and we believe that the readers of our historical notes are starting to feel similarly (or we just reinforced this feeling). We are anxiously awaiting our next stop. See you later!

notes.title: Locomotive 6-1 (The Taurus)
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28520888/2dc3fcd0790880880175e79b4766301c19fa2c8f.png[/img] Good day, train lovers! It’s been a truly exciting week for us since Train Valley 2 departed from Full Release Station, but it was but another stop. The journey continues: today we resume our trip through the history of locomotives... which is, actually, also about to reach its final destination. In our last historical vignette, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/602320/announcements/detail/1633028287880096802]we discovered[/url] a Chinese locomotive, the SS8, and with it, we closed the chapter of the first Electric Era. Today we enter the second one, which we could say started around 1995 and is pretty much still underway. If the popularization of electric-powered engines was the landmark of the previous era, in this one the most important characteristic is the constant spreading of high-speed trains, which are slowly becoming the norm for long- and medium-distance travels in Europe and Asia. 

There is no international standard as such, but trains operating over 250 km/h on new railway lines or over 150km/h in old lines are widely considered to be high-speed. They are not exactly new, though: the first one started operating in 1964 between Tokyo and Osaka. However, they weren’t really successful at the beginning. The first reason for that is its implementation costs: for a train to be high-speed they don’t just need fast and powerful locomotives, but also special rails and sometimes even new railway routes – after all, no matter how powerful your engine is, you can’t expect to go fast on a dirt track! High-speed trains are also mostly used for passenger transport, and that makes them only really efficient in highly populated areas. 

For all these reasons, they only started to spread in the 90s, and only became really popular in Europe and Asia (as we explained in a previous post, America is a different story) the first years of the 21st century. We’re still living this process: high-speed lines are still being built all over the world as of today, for instance in the Arab world, China, and even Europe. Today we discover one of the most popular trains of this era in Germany: the EuroSprinter 64 U.

[img]https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b5/DB_182_002.JPG[/img] (Photo from [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroSprinter#/media/File:DB_182_002.JPG]Wikipedia[/url])

[h1]The Eurosprinter 64 U[/h1]
The Eurosprinter is a whole family of electric locomotives built originally for the European market, but it became so popular that it spread as far as Korea, China, and the US. It’s got an important peculiarity: it’s completely modular, which facilitates its maintenance and makes it easier to customize to different lines. They are used both for passenger and freight work; its use is stated in their name: the U in 64 U stands for Universal use, while a freight Eurosprinter would wear an F (like the ES 64 F). 

The first prototype of the Eurosprinter came up in 1992, and they went to mass production in 1996. With some variations, their production stopped in 2010. Thanks to its modular nature, they’re capable of working in many different situations – for instance, they are adapted to all four European electric systems. It’s got the well-known Bo’Bo’ configuration, and it’s usually capable of reaching up to 230 km/h with a power output of 6,400 kW (that’s where the 64 in its name come from!). 

We say “usually” because the ES 64 U is officially the fastest conventional electric locomotive. In 2006, the locomotive 1216 025-5 reached a top speed of 357 km/h when doing tests before its delivery to the Austrian Federal Railways company ÖBB. This broke a record that had resisted since 1955 when SNCF's BB9004 attained 331 km/h between Lamothe and Morcenx on France

You can see the in-game counterpart of this locomotive, which features the same symmetrical appearance and its triangular side windows, and its long pantograph. It sorts of look like a two-headed snake, right? This beauty is ready to cross your best railway lines at full speed! That’s all for today! In the next post, we’ll discover a new locomotive that inspired the ones you can find in Train Valley 2, and continue our trip across the history of locomotives. Until then, we wish you a great week and a safe trip for your trains. Choo-choo! :tvloco:

notes.title: Locomotive 5-3 (The Broom)
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28520888/253944219ef5c68c53a9a8e353181bf4b08b47a6.png[/img]
Good day, train lovers! It’s been a while since the full release of Train Valley 2; for us, it’s been (and still is) a super exciting period, but we are happy and incredibly grateful for the great reception of the game. We feel humbled by your passion and love, so first of all, we want to say thanks to all of our players. We also want to say that this is the start of the journey. We’re gathering all your feedback, and rest assured, there are future stations to look forward to! 
But life (and trains) still goes on, and so do our series of historical vignettes about the real locomotives that have inspired the ones you can find and put to use in Train Valley 2. Prepare your luggage for a long, long trip, for today we’re crossing the world to the Popular Republic of China. Today we discover the SS8, a popular Chinese train – and the last one of our first generation of electric locomotives. 

[h1]A brief history of the railroad in China[/h1]
Before we dive into the locomotive of the day, it’s worth explaining a few key details about the history of rail transport in China – a history so turbulent that it helped to topple a ruling dynasty. Creating an efficient railroad network for a country so big that amounts to a whole continent is not exactly an easy endeavor – so much that we could say that they are still ongoing. On top of that, they started sort of late: by mid-19th century some top-level politicians and intellectuals called for the building of the first railways, but the very conservative Qing court rejected the idea. Apparently, they thought the steam engines were a “clever but useless” idea, and they feared the railways would eliminate natural defensive barriers and harm agriculture. 
Because of this, the very first railroads in China were built by the British in Shanghai… but since it didn’t have approval from the Qing government, it was dismantled only a year afterward. Just a few years later, the Viceroy of Zhili managed to convince the Empress Dowager to build a railway line from a coal mine to a nearby city. In order to sway her, he built a 2 kilometers railway from her residence to her dining hall. Even though, according to stories, the Empress was worried that the steam locomotive would disturb the feng shui of the imperial city and had the train pulled by eunuch slaves, in the end, she approved the construction of the railway line. 
In the next years, railway construction lived a fast development: China’s defeat in the first Sino-Japanese War convinced the government of the need for modernization – and the most powerful nations of the world were also pressing to get concessions to build railways, settlements, and mines in China. In the course of 15 years, Britain, France, Germany, the United States, Japan, Russia, and even Belgium build around 9,000 km of rails. This interference, in turn, angered the Chinese, which prompted the government to permit provinces to create local railway companies and sell shares to the public. Some of these provinces bankrupted, though, and the Qing government sought to nationalize these local companies and offer them to foreign banks in exchange for loans. 
Now hold on tight, this gets interesting. This attempt at nationalization angered the public even more, and it sparked the creation of the Railway Protection Movement. The government dispatched troops to suppress this movement. A still-secret revolutionary movement took the opportunity to launch an attack, the Wuchan Uprising. And this uprising kickstarted the Xinhai Revolution, the war that overthrew the Qing Dynasty. In a nutshell: a two-thousand years old imperial dynasty ended because they tried to take some people’s trains away. You don’t mess with train lovers! 
The first half of the 20th century was marked by World War II and the Chinese Civil War that established the Popular Republic of China. Some railways were dismantled as a war strategic measure, some others were created. In 1949, China had around 22,000 km of usable railway network – a low number for a country that big. After decades of war, the communist government rolled up their metaphorical sleeves and put themselves to work. In the first five years, 6,100 km of new railway were built. The Great Leap Forward was a mixed bag, with misguided efforts that pushed the Chinese railroad and engines beyond their capacity causing lots of accidents and problems. Ironically, they tried so hard that it actually slowed down the construction, in some places for decades. 
Despite some improvements in the system, the Cultural Revolution slowed down the building of new railways, and only new 16,000 km were set (when their initial goal was of more than 100,000 km by the 70s). During the 80s construction pretty much stopped, with government money going elsewhere – although it was also the time when steam engines were replaced by diesel and electric locomotives. And we arrive at last at the protagonist of the day, the SS8.

[img]https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/67/SS8-0191_Hunghom.jpg[/img] (Photo from [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Railways_SS8#/media/File:SS8-0191_Hunghom.jpg]Wikipedia[/url])

 [h1]China Railways SS8, the Broom[/h1]
The Shaoshan 8 (SS8 from now on) is a semi-high-speed electric locomotive, the eighth iteration of the “dynasty” of Chinese electric locomotives. Diesel and electric engines took more time to become popular in China because labor was so cheap that steam was still under use until the 80s. The first SS1 was built during the 60s; the first SS8 was produced in 1994, and it's batch production started three years later. It’s a Bo’Bo’ machine, a quite popular axle arrangement that we’ve seen in many other machines by now: two bogies with two powered axles.
Their first route was the Kingguan Line, which linked Beijing with Guangzhou; currently, it serves the Shanghai—Kowloon and the Beijing—Kowloon lines, two of the most popular lines in China (and quite long: they take 20 and 23 hours respectively). Kowloon is the old name of the train station in Hong Kong; as you surely can figure, trains from Shanghai and Beijing to Hong Kong are of key importance. The SS8 pantograph had to be adapted to access Hong Kong, and until last year it was the only electric train allowed to enter the city. Thanks to this, the SS8 is a true icon of the recent past of the Chinese railroad network. 
The SS8 was, for some time, the fastest Chinese locomotive: in 1998 it broke the Chinese speed record with a top speed of 239,6 km/h on a test run. That record lasted for some time until the popularization of high-speed trains in China during the 00s. Its nickname is “the Broom”… but to be honest, we have no idea why it is called that – maybe because it sweeps the railway leaving nothing behind? We’ve tried to find a reliable source to confirm it but we couldn’t find any, so if any of our Chinese-speaking players can clarify the story, we’ll be happy to update this blog!
And what about the in-game version of the SS8? You can see the serious-looking front, with its square windows and protruding nose, and the iconical stripped plow. The long board on its side and the pantograph are also very recognizable. This machine is used to crossing very long distances and won’t stop at anything! 

This post ends the first generation of the Electric Era; we’re getting close to the present day, with trains that still populate their countries’ railways. In the next blog of this series, we’re traveling to Germany to discover a very interesting train that you still can find easily in today’s German railways.
Stay tuned! :tvloco:

notes.title: Locomotive 5-2 (The Caiman)
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28520888/126fc135acb93235b9152dc8b63da5c51f4e4fcc.png[/img] Good day, train lovers! We’re back at our series of vignettes about the history of locomotives. Last week, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/602320/announcements/detail/1725349546518800609]we entered the Electrical Era[/url] and discovered the ChS8, a powerful machine with an unkind fate: built to be the cornerstone of long-distance passenger trains, it almost fell to oblivion after the collapse of the USSR. Today we start our historical trip going from the cold steppes of Russia and Ukraine to the warm and sunny shores of the Mediterranean sea: let’s travel to Italy! 

[h1]FS Class E-656: the Caimano[/h1]
After the Second World War, the Italian national railroad company FSI (Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane) decided to invest in new locomotives, faster and more potent. The E.626 and E.636, built during the Fascist regime, were simply not powerful enough. In 1953, the FSI started working in a new model engine meant to be mounted on the modified chassis of the E.636. Five years later, the first prototypes of the E.646 and E.645 locomotives were produced. Just a few years later they designed and built a 4-axle locomotive with a similar concept, the high-speed E.444, which would be ironically nicknamed the Tortoruga (tortoise).

The E.444 was a success, but in just a few years the FSI realized they needed new locomotives not just faster and more potent, but also more modern, adapted to modern systems of control (instead of just to the old electromechanical systems). After 40 years of service, the first Italian-made locomotives were obsolete – not to say simply limping its way after many tweaks repairs. On top of that, more modern engines such as the E.646 were less and less useful due to the increasing number of passengers after the economic recovery of the 50s and 60s, the “Italian miracle”. In order to avoid problems transitioning to a brand new type of machines, they decided not to start a design from scratch, go back to the field-tested E.636 and modernize it. The first E.656 was built in 1975; when they went out of production in 1989, a total of 461 engines had been built over the years. The E.656 has a B-B-B wheel configuration: three independent two-axle bogies, all of them individually powered by separate traction motors. It’s a rheostatic electric engine – which means that it uses a system of resistance to avoid excessive amperage at its start, thus reducing the risk of an electric overload. Funny enough, even though it is more powerful than the Tartaruga, with a +25% tractive effort, it is also significantly slower (150 km/h vs 200 km/h)… at least in ideal circumstances: in old lines, or when coupled to old coaches, the Tartaruga could not reach its max speed anyway. 

[img]https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/be/FS_E656_294.jpg[/img] (Photo from [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FS_Class_E.656#/media/File:FS_E656_294.jpg]Wikipedia[/url])

The E.656 are all-purpose locomotives and they have been used on every kind of work, from freight to passenger transport. Reliable and powerful, they are capable of hauling heavy loads in difficult terrains – of which the mountainous Italy has quite a lot. Its nickname, the Caimano (alligator) was chosen by an actual train lover, just like you: every time the FSI built a new locomotive, they called a contest in its official magazine to choose a name with the fans. Of all the entries, they liked Caimano the most – and just like it happened with the Tartaruga, they painted the animal of the new logo on the sides of the locomotives. Although with significant updates and tweaks, the Caimanos are still in service in the Italian railways. 

In the in-game counterpart of the Caimano you can see featured the same rectangular-shaped windows, the circular ones in the sides, the prominent front, and its two circular lights. The E.656 collects its power from an overhead line, so in this locomotive you can also see the pantograph in the frontal part of the roof. 

That’s it for this week’s glimpse at the history of locomotives, but we suggest you not to bring your luggage down, for in next week’s blog we’re going really far, far away, to discover the history of the railway in China and one of its locomotives. Until then, get ready for the ride, train lovers! :tv2conductor:

notes.title: Locomotive 5-1 (The Disco)
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28520888/90c8059142321635a3d26487ce58d4372e5eb6bb.png[/img] Greetings train lovers! Week after week we’ve been traveling through the history of locomotives in this series of historical posts, discovering the historical locomotives that inspired the engines that you can find in Train Valley 2. Time flies, and after reading more about the steam and diesel eras, we’re slowly approaching our present time. Today we arrive at the 80s and with them to a new generation of machines: electrical-powered locomotives. 

Should we want to go fussy over it, technically speaking diesel locos were also electrical: the diesel engines produced electricity which, in turn, powered the traction motors. But when we talk about electric engines we meant engines 100% powered by electricity, which is cheaper, safer, quieter, more efficient, and more powerful than diesel… But it has one major disadvantage: for obvious reasons, you can’t run trains with batteries. Thus, the entire railway needs to be electrified… which means that the cost of infrastructure is much higher than with diesel machines. 

When you want a train to be electrical, you need overhead lines (or an electrified rail running parallel to the actual railways), but also control and security systems to keep the whole thing running without accidents. That’s incredibly expensive, and it cannot be done in stages – you need to electrify the entire line before you can put any electrical trains in them. This means that for an electrified line to be profitable, or at least run on an acceptable deficit, it needs to have a consistently high traffic volume – and even so, the investment in this infrastructure hardly ever shows in the short-term. 
That also explains why there are still a lot of diesel trains running, especially in North America: electrifying a line is not just about economy or engineering, but also a political thing. In the US, for instance, railroad infrastructure is private, and private companies may lack the capacity (or the desire) of investing in electrification. On top of that, the US impose higher property taxes on privately owned rail facilities. In contrast to this, in pretty much the rest of the world railway networks are considered part of the key national infrastructures – they are financed by the states, which do have the capacity and motivation for such grand undertakings, and train operators pay fees for using them. 
Electric locomotives by themselves are not exactly a new invention: the first one known was built in 1837 and ran on batteries, but it couldn’t run for more than 2.4 km before running out of energy. It managed, mind you, to haul up to six tons at a surprising speed (for then) of 6km/h. Funny enough, it was quickly destroyed by railway workers who feared for their jobs – but that didn’t stop engineers from keep working on new models of electric locomotives. Back then, in spite of all their problems and technical challenges, they had a major advantage over steam: they didn’t produce smoke, which was a problem in tunnels and especially in urban areas, where coal exhaust was worsening the life of citizens. The first electrical tram opened in 1881 near Berlin; the first electrically-worked underground line started working in London in 1890. Thus, electric locomotives quickly became the standard for underground lines and tramways, easier and cheaper to electrify with the knowledge they had back then about electricity and its usage. 

The first electrical locomotives were all DC (direct current), but that meant an important problem: DC electricity can’t be transported over long distances without losing lots of energy, which made its usage out of urban areas impractical. In America, that made it somehow interesting for short sections (like mountain crossings) where coal or water was difficult to come by. That, along with the economical and political implications already mentioned, stalled the electrification of lines in America – up to the point that many lines even were dismantled. In Europe, on the other hand, the development of these engines continued. The first technical challenge that needed to be overcome in order to electrify long-distance railway was creating AC locomotives. Italy saw the first 100 % electrical mainline, and after some experiments, prototypes, and inventions by engineers such as Charles Brown and Kálmán Kandó, by the 30s electrical locomotives were ready for its widespread implementation. AC locomotives were better for crossing the many mountainous regions of Europe both because of its superior traction in steeper lines and the inherent difficulties of supplying coal at these heights and distances. Also, hydroelectric power was readily available, making electricity cheaper and easier to come by than coal and diesel. After World War II, France decided that AC locomotives performed well enough to start implementing it across all its network, regardless of terrain, until it became the standard. Taking into account that France was administrating Germany in the immediate years after the war, and its importance in Europe and in the construction of the European Union, this decision was highly influential in making electrical locomotives the European standard. 

Despite everything, such an undertaking is not exactly easy. The world was still in ruins in the post-war era; serious efforts at electrification didn’t start until the 60s. But in the next decades, electric locomotives became faster and more efficient thanks to all sorts of innovations, from a better energy usage that allowed for much more speed to regenerative braking that recovered kinetic energy during braking. And just like that, we arrived at the 80s when the development of high-speed trains motivated countries such as Italy, Germany, France, Spain, and Japan to electrify more and more lines, even building high-speed electrical lines from scratch. This is what we consider the start of the Electric Era of Locomotives. 

[h1]The ChS8 (The Disco)[/h1]
The first locomotive from this time that we are going to discover is the ChS8, a Soviet locomotive engine designed and built by  Škoda. Back then, the Czech manufacturer Skoda was still a state-owned Soviet company; the ChS8 was produced in Czechoslovakia but used mostly in Russia and Ukraine. It was an 8 axle locomotive, developed for pulling very long passenger trains at 100 km/h or faster. Thanks to this, it helped to mitigate a problem that affected the Soviet railway network since the end of the 70s: the increasing passenger traffic was in conflict with the need for high volume freight lines; since the strained Soviet economy could not afford new lines, the USSR needed existent trains to be more efficient by adding more cars. That, in turns, created the need for more powerful locomotives. 

[img]https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Locomotive_ChS8-075_2011_G1.jpg/2560px-Locomotive_ChS8-075_2011_G1.jpg[/img] (Photo from [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChS8#/media/File:Locomotive_ChS8-075_2011_G1.jpg]Wikipedia[/url])

Here enters the ChS8, the most powerful AC passenger locomotive ever designed in the USSR… which, because of the turns of history, was relatively short-lived. Three prototypes were built in 1983 and sent to Ukraine for tests and adjustments. 30 locomotives were built in 1987, 50 more in 1989… and then the USSR collapsed. In just a couple of years, the former Soviet republics had more urgent things to care about than trains. After the disintegration of the USSR, passenger turnover in Russia and Ukraine fell dramatically, so there was not a great need for such powerful locomotives. Some of them are still in service, although in the last decade the Russian railways are turning to more efficient locomotives like the EP10 and EP20. 

Here you have the in-game counterpart of the ChS8, with a similarly solid, strong, no-nonsense design. See also its two square-shaped frontal windows and its side windows, distributed in pairs except for the crew’s window and the last one. And check the roof for something you will in all this era’s locomotives: the pantograph, the apparatus that collect power from the overhead line. 
Today’s post is a great example of the close relationship between the history of trains and History in general. The ChS8 is especially interesting for appearing in such an important critical moment for people, and how it affected its implementation, usage, and final fate. 

We hope you enjoyed this story, see you next week! :tv2conductor:
